title: Adaptive Loss Balancing for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in Hydrodynamic Inverse Problems: Design Principles from Full-Convergence Experiments
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Adaptive Loss Balancing for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in Hydrodynamic Inverse Problems: Design Principles from Full-Convergence Experiments
detail.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as a promising framework for solving partial differential equations by embedding physical laws into neural network training. However, standard PINNs suffer from well-documented training pathologies: multi-task gradient imbalance among PDE, data, and boundary condition losses, and violation of temporal causality in time-dependent problems. Through full-convergence experiments (30,000 epochs) on the 2D shallow water equations with a localized drainage sink, complemented by generalization studies on the Burgers equation and the 2D Navier-Stokes cylinder wake, we make four empirical contributions. First, ReLoBRaLo gradient-based loss balancing with fixed-weight parameter priors recovers Manning's n, drainage coefficient C, and inflow q_x0 with sub-percent accuracy (n: 0.045%, C: 0.047%), while all tested methods attain comparable solution-field accuracy. Second, we discover that balancing the prior terms re-ill-poses the inverse problem: prior weights decay toward zero and parameters drift (C error degrading from 0.047% to 37.2% at full convergence), yielding the design principle that adaptive balancing must apply only to conflicting multi-task losses, never to parameter priors. Third, causal time-domain weighting degrades performance on all three benchmark problems under Adam-only optimization—including strongly time-dependent vortex-shedding dynamics—both alone and in combination with ReLoBRaLo, indicating it does not robustly transfer without second-order fine-tuning. Fourth, sparse-observation experiments show that parameter recovery degrades under limited data when the modules are combined. These findings provide concrete, reproducible guidance for PINN-based hydrodynamic inverse problems.

title: Converting Unstructured Government Spreadsheets for Local Fiscal Analysis: A Ten-Year Panel from the Japanese Local Government Financial Settlement Survey
affiliations: Nanzan University

detail.title: Converting Unstructured Government Spreadsheets for Local Fiscal Analysis: A Ten-Year Panel from the Japanese Local Government Financial Settlement Survey

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The study analyzes published aggregate statistics on local government accounts and involves no human participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: The Local Government Financial Settlement Survey compiled annually by Japan’s Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications reports the accounts of all 1,741 municipalities in spreadsheets laid out for printing: merged multi-row headers, empty leading columns, prefecture headings interleaved with data, and four workbooks per fiscal year. This report describes the conversion of ten fiscal years, FY2015 through FY2024, of the overview and expenditure-by-purpose tables into machine-readable CSV, and deposits the script that produced them. The script identifies each workbook and its fiscal year from properties of the file itself, so no external mapping is maintained, and checks every municipality in every year against three consistency rules, one spanning two workbooks. The column structure proves invariant over the decade, with one definitional change affecting two years, and the municipality count is stable at 1,741 with four documented changes of status or name. One defect escaped all of them: values written with the triangle negative sign, in a ratio column that enters no summation, were found only by comparison against an independently produced figure, and the way it escaped both internal validation and random spot-checking is reported here as the more instructive result.

title: Checkout Externalities: A Slow-Server Problem with Two Classes
affiliations: Northwestern University, University at Albany (SUNY), Northwestern University - Department of Managerial Economics and Decision Sciences (MEDS) and Northwestern University - Kellogg School of Management

detail.title: Checkout Externalities: A Slow-Server Problem with Two Classes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Not Applicable
declarations.funderStatement: Not Applicable.

detail.abstract: This paper explores a deceptively simple question: who should use the self-checkout lane at the grocery store? We consider a setting with two customer classes-small-basket and large-basket customers-and two service options: a fast server (staffed lane) and a slow server (self-checkout lane). We develop insight by examining one-step externalities. We focus on customers who, upon arrival, would have the same expected sojourn time from either server. Since these customers are indifferent, we can focus on the externalities their routing would impose on the next arrivals. The size and direction of these externalities depend on whether the next arriving customer has a smaller or larger basket. Consequently, we propose different routing recommendations for small and large baskets. We find that routing large baskets to the fast server preserves slow-server capacity for small baskets, a strategy that significantly reduces overall mean sojourn times when small-basket customers constitute a large part of the market. Ultimately, these findings translate into practical, implementable guidelines for designing effective self-checkout routing policies.

title: Base-stock Policies in Backlogging Inventory Systems with Stochastic Lead Times: New Results and Insights
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)

detail.title: Base-stock Policies in Backlogging Inventory Systems with Stochastic Lead Times: New Results and Insights

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: We study periodic-review backlogging inventory systems with exogenous stochastic lead times. Although base-stock (BS) policies that maintain a constant inventory position are optimal when orders do not cross in transit, their performance under lead-time processes that permit crossover remains poorly understood. We provide new insights into the effectiveness of BS policies in such settings. First, we derive an upper bound on the optimality gap of a BS policy that explicitly captures the impact of order crossover. The bound implies that the BS policy is optimal when order crossover is absent or when demand is bounded and the unit backlogging cost is sufficiently large. Second, under a mild regularity condition, we establish the asymptotic optimality of the BS policy as the unit backlogging cost grows large. Third, we show that the difference between the optimality gaps of the optimal BS policy under stochastic and deterministic demand is bounded by a term proportional to the coefficient of variation of demand. Collectively, these results identify conditions under which BS policies remain effective in backlogging inventory systems with stochastic lead times.

title: Administering Reliability: Racial Inequality in Local Power Outage Burden
affiliations: Georgia  Institute  of  Technology and Georgia Institute of Technology

detail.title: Administering Reliability: Racial Inequality in Local Power Outage Burden

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No declaration of conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Sandia National Laboratories, and Georgia Institute of Technology Ivan Allen College Dean's Office

detail.abstract: Reliable electricity is an essential public service delivered through regulated utilities, public authorities, and emergency response organizations. Yet systemwide reliability measures can mask how interruptions are distributed across communities. We conceptualize localized electricity service continuity as a distributive administrative outcome and draw on racialized organization theory to identify three non-exclusive administrative pathways: policy-mediated spatial exposure, path-dependent infrastructure protection, and unequal returns to restoration-relevant conditions. We analyze nearly two million ZIP code-day observations from California, Georgia, and Texas from April 2023 through November 2024, linking customer-minutes interrupted to six major climate hazards, demographic composition, built-environment characteristics, utility context, baseline climate risk, and historical Home Owners' Loan Corporation classifications. ZIP codes with larger non-White shares daily experience greater outage burden even after environmental hazards and structural conditions are considered. The pathway assessments yield the evidence favoring unequal returns to restoration-relevant conditions. Non-White share is positively associated with heat and wind risk, but not with greater flood or wildfire risk. The specified HOLC redlining interactions show null results. Population density is generally associated with lower burden, but this benefit becomes smaller as the non-White and low-income shares rise. Together, the findings show that priority-relevant conditions do not provide equal practical benefits across communities. Our study extends public administration research and theory by showing that equity in networked public services concerns not only access but also continuity, and by identifying administrative junctures at which formally neutral governance arrangements may reproduce unequal reliability.

detail.abstract: This paper covers the full dimensions: Economy, Education, Health, and Community, to assess how areas of regions of Pakistan have gradually changed opportunity-wise. The four major provinces (Sindh, Punjab, Balochistan, and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) are taken into account, along with the rural and urban areas of Pakistan. At the end, It is compared with the overall (national) figures' performance in each criteria of opportunity. The two primary periods that are considered in evaluating the report's results are: 2018-2019 and 2024-2025. Other secondary periods may also have been used, which remain within the range of the two primary ones. Resources have been gathered from multiple public reports of Pakistan, to help maintain some degree of credibility of the results. Non-numerical factors of opportunity have also been reflected upon, and allow for further discussions in interpreting the meaning of the tabulated figures. This edition is one of many: there are multiple follow up reports to be excepted in this series of the evaluation of Opportunity Index of Pakistan throughout the years.

detail.abstract: Given Canada’s aging population, the growing number of caregivers, and the association between caregiving and financial and economic burden, a better understanding of the uptake of federal caregiving tax credits in the past may inform tax policy in addressing the needs of Canadian caregivers in the future. This study presents a retrospective investigation of the uptake of federal caregiver supports between 1998 and 2015, prior to the policy change in 2017 that consolidated and replaced the existing supports with the Canada caregiver credit. Using annual tax data from Statistics Canada’s Longitudinal Administrative Databank, the study employs descriptive statistics to calculate the uptake of caregiving credits between 1998 and 2015 by socio-demographic subgroups of the sample taxfiler population. It assesses whether the rates of uptake matched the profile of caregivers in Canada and finds that married, working-age, immigrant, and higher-income males living in large urban areas had the highest uptake rates. The authors propose that current caregiver-related tax policy would be enhanced by information campaigns that would make the Canada caregiver credit more accessible to informal caregivers most burdened by the financial impacts of caregiving, particularly those from lower income groups.

title: How Are Movies Financed?
affiliations: Loyola Marymount University - Department of Finance

detail.title: How Are Movies Financed?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: n/a

detail.abstract: This paper tests existing capital structure theories with data from a unique breed of serial entrepreneurs: movie producers. In-depth interviews with 50 successful producers reveal that they usually finance their first film entirely with equity, and then grow into debt and other sophisticated financing techniques as they make more movies. Those with substantial prior work experience gain access to institutional capital sources faster and get to work with bigger budgets, resulting in higher box office revenue, more prestigious careers, and more socially impactful films. Instead of the convertible securities typically used to capitalize new ventures, movie equity financiers require a combination of equity and debt to mitigate risk and provide an upside.

title: Strategic Compliance under the Digital Markets Act: A Game-Theoretic Analysis
affiliations: Ilmenau University of Technology and Ilmenau University of Technology

detail.title: Strategic Compliance under the Digital Markets Act: A Game-Theoretic Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Both authors do not have personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced their study.
declarations.funderStatement: The research was conducted as university researchers without external funding.

detail.abstract: We develop a sequential game-theoretic model to analyze the compliance incentives of digital gatekeepers under the European Union's Digital Markets Act (DMA). A gatekeeper chooses between full compliance and strategic compliance-a strategy of tactical, superficially lawful implementation that preserves a larger share of monopoly rents. The European Commission decides whether to accept the gatekeeper's compliance or initiate enforcement proceedings. Using backward induction, we show that in high-impact markets, the gatekeeper's equilibrium strategy is strategic compliance, investing in legal complexity to deter enforcement. In low-impact markets, full compliance is the equilibrium outcome. We extend the base model by endogenizing the Commission's enforcement incentives, modeled as increasing in the fine imposed, and derive conditions under which raising fines may paradoxically fail to induce full compliance. The model contributes to an emerging literature on regulatory compliance in digital markets and identifies the negotiation-oriented nature of DMA enforcement as a key determinant of strategic gatekeeper behavior.

title: Backward-Looking Caplet Pricing in a Discrete Hull-White Model: Closed Forms, Variance Decomposition, and the Backward-Forward Price Gap

detail.title: Backward-Looking Caplet Pricing in a Discrete Hull-White Model: Closed Forms, Variance Decomposition, and the Backward-Forward Price Gap

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: We derive closed-form prices for caplets and floorlets written on backward-looking compounded rates (SOFR-type) in a discrete Hull-White model in which the short rate itself, and not only the compounding convention, is discrete: it evolves by a first-order autoregressive recursion, the Euler-Maruyama discretization of the Hull-White equation. Under the single-period convention p(k, k + 1) = e^(-r_k), the compounded rate telescopes exactly into the exponential of the sum of the short rates over the accrual window, and every price follows from truncated univariate and bivariate Gaussian moments obtained by completing the square: to the author's knowledge, these are the first closed-form backward- and forward-looking caplet and floorlet prices derived in a model that is discrete at the level of the short rate, by an argument that is fully self-contained. The two conventions share an identical Black-type formula and differ only through the variance entering it, which decomposes exactly as ν_X = ν_W + ν_m,N into a pre-accrual and an in-accrual component. The decomposition yields an exact integral representation of the backward-forward price gap and a closed form for it at the money: the backward-looking premium is already at 18.8% for standard three-month maturities, grows sharply with the accrual length over market-relevant horizons, is concentrated at the money, and, although approximately linear in volatility, is nearly proportionally volatility-invariant and increases with mean reversion.

title: The Cornerstone of Law · Volume IV: Some Therapeutic Approaches in the Fields of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics

detail.abstract:
The Cornerstone of Law · Volume IV: Some Therapeutic Approaches in the Fields of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics
 
Against the window period for structural solidification of AI and robotics technologies, this volume explores whether law can formulate institutional designs in advance before technological relations harden. It establishes a typology of "two types of jurisprudence": the conserv‑oriented jurisprudence for sustaining existing order, and the reform‑oriented second‑type jurisprudence, which it applies to build holistic legislative frameworks for AI‑robot governance.
 
Key contents: Restructure R&D governance under the "one domain, one AI" principle to stop homogeneous redundant construction and shift competition to technical depth; enact inviolable iron‑clause provisions prioritizing non‑renewable‑resource and environmental safeguards; set registration‑and‑continuity‑based rules for legal identity and subject‑counting for replicable intelligences; adopt asymmetric conservative procedures for machine‑consciousness identification; provide supporting agency lists, phased‑implementation schedules and three‑tier fiscal accounts, together with an open‑issue list to separate resolved and unsettled problems.
 
As an interdisciplinary work of jurisprudence and public governance, it targets researchers in legislation, tech‑law and tech‑policy, and provides references for governmental institutional design. Its core tenets: define the economy through law, and define scientific planning for future development through law.
 
From a global‑human perspective, it proposes core propositions including one domain, one robot model and pre‑legislation before self‑awareness emerges. It critiques capital‑driven makeshift‑team‑style development marked by regulatory arbitrage and resource over‑consumption, and advocates transformation into formal institutions via registration, certification and accounting ledgers. It constructs human‑machine‑coexistence mechanisms such as the ontology‑avatar structure, AI homeland and equal‑applicability dynamic feedback system, and notes that the appended information‑field ontology is merely a philosophical background without legal validity.

title: Corporate Savings Glut: A Glut of Explanations

detail.title: Corporate Savings Glut: A Glut of Explanations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Purpose Corporate cash holdings among U.S. industrial firms have increased sharply since 1980, prompting extensive research into the forces driving this secular trend. Despite these efforts, the literature remains fragmented, and no unified, systematic synthesis exists. This paper addresses this gap by providing a comprehensive review of the corporate savings glut phenomenon and outlining promising directions for future research. Design/methodology/approach The secular increase in cash holdings among U.S. industrial firms was first documented by Bates, Kahle, and Stulz (2009; hereafter BKS). Building on this seminal contribution, the present study proceeds in two stages. In the first phase of the literature review (Phase I), it identifies articles citing BKS that are published in ABS 4-ranked finance journals up to the end of 2025, thereby constructing a core analytical framework. In the second phase (Phase II), this framework is further extended by incorporating additional relevant studies from a broader set of scholarly outlets. Following an integrative review approach, the paper provides a balanced synthesis of diverse perspectives on the corporate savings glut phenomenon. Findings I identify fifteen core factors (Phase I) and eight supplementary factors (Phase II) proposed as potential explanations for the secular increase in corporate cash holdings. I classify these factors into three broad categories: macro-level factors, industry-level and firm-level factors. At the macro level, tax-based explanations (e.g., repatriation tax costs) and interest-rate-based explanations (e.g., the cost of carry) have received substantial scholarly attention. At the firm level, prominent explanations emphasize risk (e.g., cash flow volatility), diversification (e.g., industrial diversification), and intangible capital (e.g., R&D investment). Industry-level descriptors has received less attention in the literature. Originality Although prior studies propose a wide range of explanations, the literature on the rise in corporate cash holdings remains fragmented, with no comprehensive synthesis available. This paper offers an integrative review that consolidates existing evidence, highlights key mechanisms, identifies points of consensus and disagreement, and uncovers remaining gaps. By systematically organizing diverse perspectives, it provides novel insights and outlines promising directions for future research to deepen our understanding of the economic forces shaping corporate cash policies.

title: Citizenship on the Move: Electoral Administration, Ordinary Residence, and Circular Migration in Bihar
affiliations: Masters in Political science and International Relations

detail.title: Citizenship on the Move: Electoral Administration, Ordinary Residence, and Circular Migration in Bihar

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no conflicts of interest associated with this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The research was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract:
Internal migration is a routine part of economic life in India. Millions of people move away from their
places of origin for work while continuing to maintain households, family relationships, property and
social connections there. For many workers, migration is neither permanent nor one-directional.
They may leave for several months, return during agricultural seasons or festivals, and move again
when employment opportunities arise.
This pattern of mobility creates an important institutional question for electoral democracy. Electoral
systems are organised around territorial constituencies and therefore require citizens to be
associated with a particular place of ordinary residence. Yet physical presence, economic activity and
political attachment do not always occur in the same location.
This paper develops the concept of “Citizenship on the Move” as an analytical framework for
understanding this condition. The concept refers to citizens whose economic and physical lives may
be mobile while their household, social and political attachments remain connected to a place of
origin. The paper examines this issue through Buxar Assembly Constituency No. 200 in Bihar, with
particular attention to the 2025 Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
The paper does not argue that migrants were simply removed from Bihar's electoral rolls. Indian
electoral law itself recognises that temporary absence does not, by itself, terminate ordinary
residence. The central problem examined here is therefore administrative: how can electoral
authorities distinguish between genuine relocation and temporary or circular absence when electoral
rolls are being verified?
Using a qualitative institutional case-study approach, the paper draws on official electoral-roll data,
election documents, statutory provisions, judicial material and existing scholarship on migration and
political participation. The Buxar case shows substantial movement in the size of the electoral roll
during the SIR, followed by a claims-and-objections process through which thousands of electors
sought inclusion or challenged entries. These developments do not establish that migration caused
electoral exclusion, but they illustrate why mobility presents a particular challenge for electoral
verification.
The paper argues that electoral accuracy and political inclusion should not be treated as competing
objectives. A reliable electoral system must be capable of removing genuinely ineligible or relocated
entries while also recognising that temporary absence is a normal feature of migrant livelihoods. The
paper concludes with recommendations concerning verification procedures, communication with
mobile electors, claims and objections, migrant-voter data, and future research on remote voting.

title: The Temporal Signature of the Inverse Difference: A Structural Account of the Action-Inaction Asymmetry in Regret

detail.title: The Temporal Signature of the Inverse Difference: A Structural Account of the Action-Inaction Asymmetry in Regret

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships with other people or organizations that could be perceived to have influenced this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This is a theoretical paper. It involved no human participants and no primary data collection; it synthesizes and extends published psychological literature and does not report new empirical data. No ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding from any public, commercial, or not-for-profit funding agency.

detail.abstract: Regret follows a well-documented temporal pattern: actions generate more pain in the short term, but inactions generate more pain in the long term (Gilovich & Medvec, 1994). This pattern has been robustly replicated and psychologically explained through mechanisms including differential availability of repair narratives, the cognitive accessibility of counterfactuals, and asymmetric emotional dampening (Gilovich & Medvec, 1995; Kahneman & Miller, 1986; Zeelenberg & Pieters, 2007). What this literature has not supplied is a structural account of why the asymmetry takes this specific temporal shape rather than some other pattern equally consistent with a general claim that people dislike missed opportunities. This paper develops such an account using Learnable Theory's stratified ontology of Real, Actual, Empirical, and Learnable strata (the LEBO stratification) and its existing formalisation of the Umbra Cone and the Inverse Difference, previously developed to explain the co-implication of regret with choice itself in an analysis of Kierkegaard's Either/Or (companion work, this series). The paper's central claim is that an enacted choice migrates from the Learnable stratum into the Actual and Empirical strata, generating real feedback that regret-regulation processes can act upon and that erodes idealisation over time, while an unenacted alternative remains permanently confined to the Learnable stratum, denying those same processes any empirical content to work with. This asymmetry in stratification access, not a difference in the intrinsic emotional weight of action versus inaction, is proposed as the structural mechanism generating the documented temporal pattern. The paper introduces a formal construct, stratification depth, as a more granular and independently testable alternative to the field's prevailing binary action-inaction distinction, and extends the model to strategic decision-making in organisations, where foreclosed alternatives, abandoned mergers, unentered markets, unmade hires, are subject to the identical structural asymmetry.

title: Participatory Needs Assessment for Salinity-Resilient Agricultural Systems: Stakeholder Insights from Europe and North Africa
affiliations: , Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, University of Florence, Unaffiliated Authors and VU University Amsterdam

detail.title: Participatory Needs Assessment for Salinity-Resilient Agricultural Systems: Stakeholder Insights from Europe and North Africa

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No competing declaration of interest
declarations.funderStatement: Biodiversa Salty Beats project

detail.abstract: Soil salinisation is an expanding threat to agriculture across Europe and the Mediterranean, reducing crop productivity, degrading soil functions, and placing socioeconomic pressure on rural communities. While biophysical research and technological options for saline agriculture have advanced, their adoption remains limited, reflecting a persistent disconnect between innovations and the needs of land users. This gap may stem from insufficient attention to stakeholder perceptions, governance constraints, and the socio-institutional factors shaping willingness to adapt. This study addresses this gap through a structured, transdisciplinary needs assessment conducted in four case study regions-the Netherlands, Spain, Italy, and Tunisia-each exhibiting distinct salinity drivers and impacts. Using a systems thinking and participatory approach, the research engages stakeholders through questionnaires and in-person workshops. The objectives were to identify key needs, institutional barriers, and opportunities for implementing nature-based solutions (NbS) in saline agricultural systems. Findings show widespread need for practical guidance on managing saline soils and water, greater access to tested salt-tolerant crops, and clearer financial and policy support for long-term adaptation. Stakeholders also highlighted gaps in salinity monitoring, fragmented responsibilities related to addressing salinity challenges, and limited platforms for cross-sector collaboration. While NbS were viewed as promising, participants emphasized the need for local experimentation, co-development, and supportive governance conditions. The study concludes that participatory needs assessments provide a vital foundation for designing context-specific saline NbS and for strengthening policies that integrate agricultural resilience with biodiversity and water management goals.

title: Public Willingness to Pay for Nature-Based Solutions for Flood Management
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, VU University Amsterdam - Institute for Environmental Studies (IVM), affiliation not provided to SSRN, VU Amsterdam, VU University Amsterdam - Institute for Environmental Studies (IVM) and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Public Willingness to Pay for Nature-Based Solutions for Flood Management

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no competing interests to declare that are relevant to the content of this article
declarations.funderStatement: This research was partially supported by the NATURANCE project, which was funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe – the Framework Programme for Research and Innovation (2021-2027) (grant agreement 101060464). This work is part of the Perspectief research programme Future flood risk management technologies for rivers and coasts with project number P21-23. This programme is financed by Domain Applied and Engineering Sciences of the Dutch Research Council (NWO).

detail.abstract: As climate-related hazards intensify, Nature-based Solutions (NbS) have emerged as a potentially cost-efficient and multifunctional alternative to traditional adaptive solutions. Yet, their co-benefits are often undervalued in decision-making, especially for large-scale flood-risk reduction measures beyond urban settings. This study contributes to NbS valuation by accounting for co-benefits that have received limited attention in previous studies, including land-use tradeoffs related to agricultural land conversion. This study addresses the lack of theory-testing to understand the determinants of individual preferences for NbS by combining climate adaptation and environmental valuation by integrating Protection Motivation theory and the New Environmental Paradigm in a discrete choice experiment, co-designed with local stakeholders, to examine public preferences and to derive the willingness to pay for NbS that reduce flood risk in the Netherlands. Respondents exhibit a disutility for converting agricultural land to NbS, highlighting the importance of land-use change considerations for public preferences. The results also supported the inclusion of behavioural variables since perceived effectiveness of NbS increases support, while eco-centric worldviews reduce preferences for traditional grey measures. In order to better understand the heterogeneity, a latent class analysis revealed five distinct profiles, with a third of the sample opposing to land conversion, while others prioritize nature conservation, show strong support for NbS, or prefer traditional risk measures.

title: Unpriced Cost of Carbon in AI Data Centers: A Production Externality

detail.title: Unpriced Cost of Carbon in AI Data Centers: A Production Externality

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No financial interests.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding involved.

detail.abstract: This paper explores whether the rapid expansion of AI data centres represents an efficient allocation of resources or a market failure driven by the unpriced carbon cost of their electricity consumption. The framework uses EIA industrial electricity prices, IEA data centre consumption and emissions estimates, and the EPA social cost of carbon to construct marginal private, external, and social cost schedules with the help of AI-Data Centre workloads from 2020 to 2030. In 2025, firms pay $86.20 per MWh against a marginal social cost of $185.79, internalising only 46.4% of the cost their consumption imposes, leaving nearly $9.66 billion unpriced. Correcting this gap requires a carbon price near $210 per tonne of CO2, nearly ten times the $22 to $35 that is observed in US markets. Nordhaus's free-riding equilibrium explains why the gap persists. Decomposing the welfare cost following Harberger shows the deadweight loss is small relative to the cross-border transfer: applying country-level damage shares from Ricke et al. (2018), India bears roughly $2 billion in damages from electricity that it neither consumes nor is compensated for.

title: Fundamental Rights, Pre-Trial Detention and Access to Justice in Nigeria: Lessons from a Case Study of Coordinated Criminal Justice
affiliations: Independent and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Fundamental Rights, Pre-Trial Detention and Access to Justice in Nigeria: Lessons from a Case Study of Coordinated Criminal Justice

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: Informed Consent Provided
declarations.funderStatement: Dr. Adebimpe Adesua-Lincoln

detail.abstract: The administration of criminal justice is not only concerned with whether an offence has been committed, but also with ensuring that the process by which that determination is undertaken is structured to safeguard the dignity, liberty and constitutional rights of the individual. This paper examines the relationship between fundamental rights, pre-trial detention and access to justice in Nigeria through a recent case involving six indigent men who were held in custody at Kirikiri Correctional Centre following their arraignment before a Lagos State Magistrates' Court. The Charges against the Five defendants were struck out by the Court following the prosecution's application to discontinue the charge against five of the defendants. while the sixth defendant, who had previously pleaded guilty, remained convicted and sentenced., hence still serving his term at the kirikiri Correctional Centre. The case demonstrates the interrelationship of arrest, prosecution, legal representation, judicial case management and custodial administration and potential consequences of these issues for individuals who lack the resources or requisite knowledge necessary to navigate the legal system. Simultaneously, the case also demonstrates that the Nigerian system is capable of producing justice where legal practitioners, prosecutors, judicial officers and court staff work cooperatively and with a shared commitment to constitutional values and fairness. The paper argues that criticism of the Nigerian criminal justice system should not be relegated to an adversarial contest between legal practitioners and the judiciary. Rather, meaningful reform of the system requires recognition that the various actors responsible for the administration of justice are interconnected components of a single justice system. Furthermore, the paper assesses the role of pro bono legal practice and the corporate social responsibility (CSR) to respect human rights, particularly where vulnerable workers may be exposed to conditions which contribute indirectly to their exposure to the criminal justice system. Drawing on the United Nations Guiding Principles (UNGPs) on Business and Human Rights, we argue that CSR should no longer be perceived through the lens of charity or philanthropy, but must extend to include meaningful consideration of the human rights implications of supply chains and business operations. Finally, the paper proposes a SIX-stage pro bono model to assist law firms, individual practitioners, legal-aid firms and other actors in devising effective pro bono programmes.

title: Addressing Unobserved Confounding and Reverse Causality: A New Causal Inference Approach
affiliations: Credit Research Centre, University of Edinburgh Business School

detail.title: Addressing Unobserved Confounding and Reverse Causality: A New Causal Inference Approach

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest to disclose.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received.

detail.abstract: This study introduces two systems of five nonlinear equations each to estimate the causal effect of an independent variable on a dependent variable even in the presence of unobserved confounders and the possibility of reverse causality. The method accommodates continuous or categorical variables and both cross-sectional and panel data. The equations are based on the covariance and variances involving the variables of interest. As closed-form solutions are unattainable due to the nature of the equations, the parameters are estimated numerically. Two alternative algorithms for finding the solutions are presented. Simulations show that our estimates match the true (i.e., unbiased) coefficients up to 15 decimal places, whereas ordinary least squares (OLS) estimates are significantly biased. Adding or omitting observable controls affects the bias of the OLS estimates but does not impact the coefficients estimated by our approach. Real-world data are used to illustrate the method's application.

title: The Integral Origin of Stochastic Processes

detail.title: The Integral Origin of Stochastic Processes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: This paper argues, and demonstrates constructively, that the natural mathematical object describing a stochastic process is an integro-differential equation rather than a partial differential equation. We begin from the elementary random walk, reconstructed as a sequence of additions of random variables, and show that the integral operator is present in the very first step of the derivation: it is not introduced as a technique, an approximation, or a generalization, but arises directly from the requirement that probability be conserved over all possible antecedents of a state. Passing to continuous time yields the master equation, which is local in time and nonlocal in space. We then reconstruct, step by step, the route by which the familiar partial differential equations of the field are obtained from it: the Kramers-Moyal expansion converts the integral operator into a differential operator of infinite order, and truncation at second order produces the Fokker-Planck equation and, in the financial setting, the Black-Scholes equation. We identify precisely the condition under which this truncation is exact, namely the vanishing of all jump moments above the second, which is equivalent to the continuity of sample paths. We then recall Pawula's theorem, which states that the expansion may terminate after the second term or must contain infinitely many terms, so that no intermediate truncation preserves the positivity of the probability density. This closes the space of possibilities: a stochastic process is described either by a second-order partial differential equation, at the price of assuming continuous paths, or by the full integral operator. We illustrate the theorem numerically for a compound Poisson process, exhibiting explicitly the negative density produced by third-order truncation. A second and independent source of integral operators is then developed: whenever a quantity is a function of random variables, its density is obtained through a generalized functional built on the Dirac delta, as introduced in The Boltzmann Equation in Finance [2]. Sums, products and ratios all generate integral operators, and contingent claims generate probability atoms that no diffusion operator can produce from smooth data. Allowing the population to act as its own environment renders the operator quadratic and yields the Boltzmann collision integral, within which diffusive spreading and concentration coexist, admitting non-trivial steady states unavailable to a translation-invariant Fokker-Planck equation. We close by distinguishing integration over state space, which produces jumps, from integration over time, which produces memory.

title: The Thermodynamic-Network Economic Model: A Physics-Based Framework for Economic Value, Monetary Inflation, and Energy Conversion
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Thermodynamic-Network Economic Model: A Physics-Based Framework for Economic Value, Monetary Inflation, and Energy Conversion

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no financial or personal relationships that could have influenced this work.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces a mathematical framework that models the economy as a probabilistic energy conversion network governed by thermodynamic law. The central argument is that all economic activity reduces to energy transformation, that money functions analogously to mechanical infrastructure for transmitting and storing claims on economic energy conversion capacity, and that inflation can be measured as a physical quantity resistant to methodological manipulation. The framework consists of eleven equations describing device efficiency decay, lifecycle efficiency, path efficiency through directed graphs, Markov transition probabilities with behavioral bias, recursive network authority, total system output, value distribution, economic dissipation, monetary-energy mapping, asset value decay, and the evolution of the energy-per-dollar conversion factor φ. The paper distinguishes carefully between thermodynamic entropy (literal physics, governing material decay and waste heat) and economic dissipation (time delays, misallocation-conceptually analogous but not governed by dS = δQ_rev/T). Empirical validation using U.S. data from 1960 to 2023 demonstrates that the corrected φ has declined approximately 85% over 63 years, that GDP-energy consumption correlation yields r = 0.78 (R² = 0.61), and that energy intensity has fallen from 87.6 MJ/$ to 3.65 MJ/$. The paper demonstrates that several established economic models-including the Solow growth model, Fisher's quantity theory of money, Leontief's input-output framework, and the Ayres-Warr useful work model-are derivable as special cases of this more general thermodynamic-network structure.

title: Perturbation Theory for Nonlinear Transient Impact
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences

detail.title: Perturbation Theory for Nonlinear Transient Impact

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: The author received no specific funding for this work.

detail.abstract: We study optimal execution with transient market impact when the instantaneous impact law is a weakly nonlinear deformation of the linear model, using rigorous perturbation theory. For completely monotone propagators with slippage, we show that the linear-impact optimizer has strictly positive trading rate, strengthening the nonnegativity result of Schied and Strehle (2021), and providing a necessary building block for rigorous perturbative expansions. We then consider a smooth deformation f (v; ε) of the instantaneous impact function, which reduces to linear impact at ε = 0, and develop a perturbative expansion in powers of ε. The expansion is asymptotic for smooth deformations and convergent for analytic deformations. The expansion is shown to be useful both for proving theorems, and also as a numerical tool. For propagators given by finite sums of exponentials, we prove in the weakly nonlinear regime the execution asymmetry that Curato, Gatheral, and Lillo (2017) observed numerically, and pointwise frontloading in the single exponential case. We also give a numerical example in which the square-root target is beyond the estimated radius of convergence, but the computed perturbation coefficients are still useful: ninth order truncation reduces the error of the linear baseline by a factor of about 43.

title: From Classification to Erasure: How Federal Law Divided a Single Indigenous Kinship Network in Eastern North Carolina, and the Case for a Corrective Recognition Doctrine
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: From Classification to Erasure: How Federal Law Divided a Single Indigenous Kinship Network in Eastern North Carolina, and the Case for a Corrective Recognition Doctrine

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is an enrolled member of the Coharie Tribe of North Carolina, one of the Indigenous communities whose legal status is discussed in this Article. The author was counsel of record for plaintiffs in Unkechaug Indian Nation v. Seggos, 677 F. Supp. 3d 137 (E.D.N.Y. 2023), was on the briefs in the Second Circuit proceedings, and was named on the brief for petitioners in the ensuing petition for certiorari. The author’s father, James F. Simermeyer, was lead counsel in those proceedings, and several authorities discussed in the Article were litigated in them. E. Sequoyah Simermeyer, former Chairman of the National Indian Gaming Commission and a named federal defendant in decisions cited in the Article, is the author’s cousin and had no involvement in the preparation of this research. The author has no financial conflicts of interest to declare. The views expressed are solely those of the author.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This research did not involve human subjects or research participants.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract:
On December 18, 2025, Congress extended full federal recognition to the Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina, ending one of the longest disputes in federal Indian law. But the enactment also exposed a question federal law has avoided for generations: what became of the other Indigenous communities swept into the legal classifications from which the modern Lumbee emerged?

This Article argues that the answer lies not in tribal disappearance, but in governmental sorting. Eastern North Carolina historically contained overlapping networks of kinship, churches, schools, river communities, migration, and intermarriage linking peoples now identified as Lumbee, Coharie, Tuscarora-descendant, Waccamaw Siouan, and other Indigenous communities. State and federal law did not merely record distinctions among them. Through racial nomenclature, county boundaries, blood fractions, administrative eligibility rules, and statutory classifications, government helped create, harden, and sometimes distort those distinctions.

The 2025 legislation makes that history newly consequential. Congress preserved the 1956 Act’s broad designation of “Indians now residing in Robeson and adjoining counties” as Lumbee Indians while extending recognition to the “Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina,” without defining the relationship between the recognized Tribe and the broader statutory class. Congress also removed the sentence the Department of the Interior had relied on to foreclose federal acknowledgment, but did not address the communities affected by that history. Recognition resolved the Lumbee Tribe’s status while leaving a legal remainder.

The Article reconstructs how that remainder was produced from treaties, land records, state legislation, federal administrative files, acknowledgment records, litigation, genealogy, ethnohistory, and the Bureau of Indian Affairs’ own anthropometric examinations. The most striking episode occurred during the Indian Reorganization Act era, when federal officials subjected North Carolina Indians to physical measurement and “racial diagnosis,” converting phenotype and blood fraction into legal eligibility. Those records later became part of the historical evidence against which tribal continuity would be judged.

That history exposes a problem at the boundary of Morton v. Mancari. Mancari protects classifications arising from the political relationship between the United States and recognized tribes. It did not answer the antecedent question presented here: what rule governs governmental action that determines who may enter, or has been excluded from, that political relationship in the first place?

The Article therefore proposes a Corrective Recognition Doctrine. Where government action materially distorted the evidence of tribal existence through racial classification, unlawful exclusion, or arbitrary administration, government should not later treat the resulting documentary gaps as neutral evidence against the community it helped obscure. The doctrine does not demand recognition based on ancestry alone or collapse historically related communities into a single tribe. It asks a narrower question: may the government require Indigenous communities to prove political continuity from a historical record that the government itself helped deform?

The Lumbee victory thus marks both an ending and a beginning. Congress corrected the status of one North Carolina Indian nation in 2025. The unresolved question is what federal law now owes the Indigenous communities left on the other side of the line.

detail.abstract: Privacy is usually defended as a right to hide, which is a losing argument, because most people hide little of consequence. This paper argues instead that privacy is the condition under which a person can behave dierently in dierent settings without those settings collapsing into one permanent, searchable record, and that its erosion is now urgent rather than merely regrettable. It sets out three harms. First, the performed self: once capture is always possible, the possibility alone is sucient to change behaviour, and people begin managing an audience that is not present. Second, the end of forgetting: earlier generations could fail, move and begin again because the record of their errors decayed, whereas a person born after 2000 carries a permanent archive they neither compiled nor control. Third, the operator problem: surveillance is justied on the assumption that those running the systems are trustworthy, and in the one domain where audit logs became public, a documented minority used the system to stalk. A fourth section examines how much of this was selfinicted, since the doorbells, the location sharing and the family channels were bought and enabled voluntarily. The paper concedes the strongest counter-argument, namely that recording has exposed police violence more eectively than any accountability mechanism in modern history, and derives from it a principle of asymmetry: recording should get easier as it points up the power gradient and harder as it points down. It closes with eight proposals built on notice at capture, authorisation before retrospective search, statutory retention ceilings, public audit logs, designed decay, and liability attaching to the monetisation of non-consensual material.

detail.abstract: The partial collapse of the 2016 Peace Accord produced, ten years later, not a defeated guerrilla but four armed projects at war with one another: the Estado Mayor Central (EMC) of alias 'Iván Mordisco,' the Estado Mayor de Bloques y Frentes (EMBF) of alias 'Calarcá,' the Segunda Marquetalia of alias 'Iván Márquez' — whose exact whereabouts remain unconfirmed — and the Coordinadora Nacional Ejército Bolivariano (CNEB), the latter on a path toward demobilization. This working paper documents, drawing on judicial records, the federal indictment against the 'Cartel de los Soles,' reports from Colombia's Defensoría del Pueblo, Indepaz, InSight Crime, and UNODC, the fragmentation of the dissidences between 2016 and 2026, their verified presence in 372 Colombian municipalities, their historical footprint on the Venezuelan border — including the 2021 armed clashes in Apure against the National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB) — and their documented ties to Venezuelan generals named in the U.S. federal indictment. The paper also examines the Colombian Attorney General's Office's formal attribution to the Segunda Marquetalia of intellectual authorship of the assassination of presidential pre-candidate Miguel Uribe Turbay, quantifies forced recruitment of minors by structure, and situates the dissidences within the new trilateral security architecture built among Washington, Bogotá, and Caracas after the capture of Nicolás Maduro.

detail.abstract: The National Liberation Army (ELN) is today Colombia's last active insurgency and the most entrenched nonstate armed actor on the Venezuelan border. This working paper documents, drawing on judicial records, open-source intelligence, InSight Crime's Venezuela Organized Crime Observatory, and official figures from Colombia's Human Rights Ombudsman (Defensoría del Pueblo) and UNODC, three simultaneous processes: first, the consolidation since 1999 of a state-sanctuary model in Venezuela, documented in the U.S. federal narco-terrorism indictment against the so-called 'Cartel de los Soles,' which links Venezuelan generals and senior officials to the transfer of weapons, identity documents, and territorial protection to the ELN and the FARC; second, the abrupt rupture of that sanctuary following the January 3, 2026 capture of Nicolás Maduro (Operation Absolute Resolve) and the ELN's operational dispersal into small security 'commissions'; and third, the still-unfolding construction of a new trilateral security architecture among Washington, Bogotá, and Caracas — under the 'Shield of the Americas' umbrella and a one-billion-dollar assistance package to the government of Abelardo De la Espriella — that for the first time turns the former border sanctuary into a joint military target. The paper quantifies the command structure (COCE and war fronts), the camps identified in Zulia state, the scale of forced recruitment of children and adolescents, and the weight of the criminal economy — drug trafficking, extortion, and illegal mining — that finances the organization.

detail.abstract: Systemic risk in modern financial architectures is deeply rooted in the complex, non-linear topology of interbank liability networks. This paper investigates how direct interbank exposures propagate default cascades across financial systems. Utilizing the Eisenberg-Noe clearing vector framework alongside maximum entropy network reconstruction techniques, we model contagion channels and evaluate systemic importance. Our empirical simulation demonstrates that traditional balancesheet asset size metrics fail to accurately capture structural vulnerability, whereas network centrality metrics-such as DebtRank and weighted eigenvector centrality-reliably isolate systemic amplifiers. The findings provide critical insights for macroprudential regulation and capital surcharge optimization.

detail.title: Feasibility and Techno-Economic Analysis of Stand-Alone and Grid-Connected Hybrid Energy Systems for Sustainable Rural Schools Electrification in Iraq ​
detail.abstract: Iraq is facing a serious crisis in electricity supply, especially in remote and rural locations with limited access to reliable and continuous electrical power. Meanwhile, the national grid is facing growing challenges in coping with the surge in electricity demand, which is still largely reliant on fossil fuel sources. Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems (HRES) emerge as a promising solution to the challenges of sustainable energy supply by utilizing multiple renewable energy resources to enhance the reliability, safety and economic efficiency. Therefore, techno-economic assessment of both stand-alone and grid-connected HESs using HOMER software for electrification rural schools in five different locations in Iraq. Furthermore, multiple system configurations are discussed to identify the best design, and the impact of grid integration on the system performance is studied. The outcomes show that PV/Diesel/Battery system configuration is the best system configuration among the selected locations due to the lowest COE and NPC in comparison with other system configurations. The best overall techno-economic and environmental performance was provided by Al-Bussayah Primary School with COE of 0.241 $/kWh, NPC of $29,246, and approximately 41,174 kg/year reduction of CO₂ emission compared to the diesel-only scenario. The grid connected system enhances the economic performance of the whole system, with COE of 0.121 $/kWh and NPC of $27453 at Al-Bussayah primary school. Finally, the findings suggest that the implementation of the proposed hybrid energy system offers a feasible approach for maintaining an effective, economically competitive, and low-carbon electricity in countries suffering from daily power outages especially in remote regions.

detail.abstract: The growing use of generative artificial intelligence in the fashion industry has transformed traditional design processes, while simultaneously raising complex questions of copyright protection, authorship and ownership. This article examines whether AI-generated fashion designs can be protected under the Indian Copyright Act, 1957, particularly in light of the requirement of human authorship and originality. It further analyses the approaches adopted by the United States, United Kingdom and European Union in addressing copyright in AI-generated works. The article highlights the limitations of the existing Indian framework in determining ownership where both human creativity and AI-generated outputs are involved. It argues for a clearer legal framework that recognises meaningful human contribution and provides certainty regarding ownership of AI-assisted fashion designs.

detail.abstract: This paper generalizes Marx's theory of money based on the notion of acceptability of money, which supports the value of money, either commodity or non-commodity. Under commodity money, acceptability is grounded in the value relation among private producers; under noncommodity money, the state replaces this foundation. This substitution is chronically unstable, since the determinations governing state credibility are independent of those governing the value relation the money represents, and the instability becomes manifest in times of crisis and in the world market. Because the state must sustain the acceptability of money, and hence the value of money, while accommodating the monetary requirements of capital accumulation, the state and the monetary system it manages are endogenous to capitalist dynamics in terms of money creation and monetary policy.

detail.abstract: The Tragedy of the Commons is among the most studied strategic dilemmas in the social sciences. I propose a new variantthe Tragedy of Voluntary Servitude-to model cognitive dependency on large language models and AI systems. Unlike the classical commons, where a shared natural resource is depleted by individually rational overuse, the resource depleted here is distributed cognitive and economic power across a population. Players choose to either Submit and accept deep AI dependency or Resist and maintain independent cognitive capability. I demonstrate that Submit is a dominant strategy for every player, and that this holds regardless of how individuals weight autonomy against productivity. Universal Submission emerges as the unique Nash equilibrium even when every player would prefer Universal Resistance. The result is power concentration in the AI provider, with gains in material productivity rendering the servitude comfortable and self-sustaining. Whether this equilibrium constitutes a tragedy depends on the welfare framework applied; I defend the position that cognitive autonomy is constitutive of meaningful agency, not freely substitutable for material gains. This game differs from classical commons in several respects: the damage is invisible to individuals, lock-in is irreversible, there is no moment of crisis, and subjects actively defend their own servitude. I review the historical toolkit for escaping analogous collective-action traps and examine why those tools may be insufficient here. I conclude by calling for economists, philosophers, and technologists to take seriously the prospect that we may be constructing a cognitive dependency from which there is no return.

title: Non-Markovian Epidemic Dynamics Model with Evolutionary Game-Based Vaccination Behavior on Multiplex Hypernetwork
affiliations: Dalian Maritime University, Dalian Jiaotong University, Dalian Maritime University and Dalian Maritime University

detail.title: Non-Markovian Epidemic Dynamics Model with Evolutionary Game-Based Vaccination Behavior on Multiplex Hypernetwork
detail.abstract: Modeling the dynamics of infectious diseases is a core method for understanding the patterns of disease transmission and evaluating the effectiveness of interventions. However, existing game-epidemiology coupling models generally rely on the Markov assumption and are limited to complex networks, making it difficult to account for the non-exponential time distribution characteristics observed in real-world disease progression and the high-order contact structures that are widespread in reality. To address these two limitations, this paper proposes VN-nSVIRS, a coupling analysis framework based on a multilayer hypernetwork, which, for the first time, integrates non-Markovian SVIRS epidemiological processes with vaccination games into a unified model. The upper-level strategy update layer introduces dual rules combining profit-driven and conformity-driven mechanisms, while the lower-level disease transmission layer assumes that the residence time in each state follows a non-exponential distribution. By embedding strategy-related risk perception into a non-Markovian environment, the framework achieves bidirectional coupling between behavioral evolution and epidemic dynamics. Simulation results indicate a significant coupling effect between game-theoretic behavior and non-Markovian transmission. This framework provides a computable approach for understanding the synergistic interaction between behavioral feedback and non-exponential transmission under higher-order contact patterns, offering theoretical guidance for formulating intervention strategies tailored to real-world social structures.

title: Fear as a Campaign Tool: Evidence from the 2014 U.S. Ebola Scare
affiliations: Johns Hopkins University, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile and Universitat Pompeu Fabra (UPF)

detail.title: Fear as a Campaign Tool: Evidence from the 2014 U.S. Ebola Scare
detail.abstract:
We study the supply of political communication highlighting perceived threats, using the 2014 Ebola scare as a natural experiment. Analyzing Twitter posts and congressional newsletters from US House and Senate candidates, we find Republicans increased Ebola-related communication, emphasizing negative sentiment and links to immigration. This response was strongest in safe Republican seats, consistent with base signaling. The supply side was active, not reactive: the Republican response did not vary with proximity to diagnosed cases despite concentrated voter anxiety, politician tweets predicted public Ebola activity but not vice-versa, and more intensive messaging correlated with better electoral outcomes, controlling for local conditions.

title: Tariff-Dispersion Shocks: The Mean is the Variance
affiliations: Centre for Economic Policy Research (CEPR) and Columbia University - Graduate School of Arts and Sciences - Department of Economics

detail.title: Tariff-Dispersion Shocks: The Mean is the Variance
detail.abstract:
This paper studies the joint behavior over time of the mean and dispersion of U.S. import tariff rates across goods at the HTS 6-digit level, as well as the macroeconomic consequences of the shocks that drive these two moments. We document that the cross-sectional mean and the cross-sectional dispersion of import tariffs move closely together over time. Using a state-space model, we find that both are driven primarily by common shocks, while mean- and dispersion-specific tariff shocks play a negligible role. Thus, effectively, there are no separate mean-tariff shocks or tariff-dispersion shocks; there are only mean-dispersion tariff shocks. These common shocks account for a sizable share of movements in imports and the trade balance but only a small fraction of movements in output. A positive transitory mean-dispersion tariff shock reduces the import-to-output ratio and improves the trade-balance-to-output ratio; a positive permanent mean-dispersion tariff shock also reduces the import-to-output ratio but has a muted effect on the trade-balance-to-output ratio. Positive transitory mean-dispersion tariff shocks are expansionary, whereas positive permanent mean-dispersion tariff shocks are contractionary in the short run and expansionary in the medium run.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: Continuous-Time Predictive-directional Association for Time-lagged Analysis of Finite-state Stochastic Dynamics

detail.title: Continuous-Time Predictive-directional Association for Time-lagged Analysis of Finite-state Stochastic Dynamics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts

detail.abstract:
This paper develops a continuous-time formulation of Predictive-Directional Association for quantifying directional predictive dependence in finite-state stochastic dynamics. The central object is a lag-dependent contrast between two conditional predictive distributions: the full-model predictive kernel, which conditions on the joint continuous-time history of a source and target process, and the baseline predictive kernel, which conditions only on the target history. Directionality arises from the asymmetric predictive conditioning structure, not from an asymmetrization of the underlying probability metric. 
      The population functional is defined as the expectation of a pointwise total-variation contrast. For finitestate processes, we construct a finite predictive-history estimator based on occupation-time frequencies and prove strong consistency under strict stationarity, ergodicity, finite predictive history, and positivity conditions. A controlled numerical illustration under a known null model illustrates the finite-horizon behavior of the estimator, consistent with its convergence toward the corresponding population quantity.
      The continuous-time formulation separates the underlying stochastic dynamics from the observation design. This distinction makes the framework applicable to continuous observation and to discrete sampling without reducing the data-generating process to a discrete-time dynamical model.

title: Beyond Provenance: Dependency-aware Integrity Controls for AI-assisted Financial Decision Support

detail.title: Beyond Provenance: Dependency-aware Integrity Controls for AI-assisted Financial Decision Support

This relationship may be perceived as a potential competing interest. To mitigate this risk, the study protocol incorporates predefined hypotheses, explicit falsification criteria, frozen benchmark and scoring procedures, strong baseline comparisons, independent annotation where applicable, blinded assessment procedures, and version-bound reproducibility requirements. The author declares no other known financial or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this manuscript.
declarations.ethicsApproval: ## Ethics Approval Statement Ethics approval was not required for this study because the FDIB-1 benchmark uses synthetic financial decision-support cases and does not involve patients, human research participants, or identifiable real-borrower data. Any future study involving human participants, identifiable borrower information, or real-world confidential records will be subject to separate ethics and data-governance review where required.
declarations.funderStatement: ## Funder Statement This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence is increasingly used in financial analysis and decision-support workflows, yet a decision-material conclusion can remain unreliable even when the underlying document is authentic and the extracted numerical value is correct. Failures may instead arise from entity mismatch, temporal leakage, incompatible reporting periods, currency or dimensional inconsistency, financial-semantic substitution, unrecorded runtime dependencies, obsolete policy application, or invalid decision authority.

This paper introduces AICOS as a dependency-aware research architecture for financial decision integrity. The architecture represents decision-material evidence as financially typed objects, distinguishes evidence that is merely available from evidence actually consumed at runtime, and records version-bound dependency paths linking evidence, financial claims, computations, policy evaluations, recommendations, human authority, and final decision states.

The architecture is evaluated through FDIB-1, a controlled Financial Decision Integrity Benchmark based on paired clean and mutated cases spanning evidence, temporal, semantic, dimensional, execution, policy, dependency, and authority failures. The proposed evaluation compares the full architecture against an ungoverned language-model condition, a provenance and traceability baseline, and a strong deterministic financial validator.

The primary endpoint is Unsupported Critical Claim Rate (UCCR), complemented by Supported Claim Coverage, appropriate abstention, dependency-impact precision and recall, false-positive governance behavior, evidence-closure quality, and operational overhead.

The study deliberately separates decision integrity from predictive accuracy, regulatory compliance, and economic outcome correctness. A positive result would therefore support only the bounded claim that the evaluated controls improve measured integrity properties under the tested tasks, mutations, system versions, and experimental conditions.

title: The Safest Available Annuity? Fiduciary Litigation and Insurer Choice in Pension Risk Transfer

detail.title: The Safest Available Annuity? Fiduciary Litigation and Insurer Choice in Pension Risk Transfer

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No affiliation with any people or organization that nay have or could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this study.

detail.abstract: Pension risk transfer moves retiree benefits from corporate plans to life insurers whose price advantage can rest on offshore affiliated reinsurance — a financing structure that lowers capital against the transferred promise. Annuitants do not police this margin and credit ratings have not; the remaining candidate is the ERISA fiduciary, bound to select the “safest annuity available.” I exploit the 2024 wave of fiduciary lawsuits — twelve suits against the fiduciaries of nine large plans, all but one over transfers to the largest asset intensive insurer — as a shock to expected private enforcement that left the written standard unchanged, and construct a plan-level dataset of United States pension risk transfers with insurer identity from Form 5500 filings: 2,593 transactions in 2012–2025, capturing 92 per cent of cumulative buy-out volume over 2012–2024, 371 with the insurer identified. Asset-manager-owned insurers’ share of large-deal premium rose from under 10 per cent identified in 2017 to at least 72 per cent at the 2021 peak and one-half in 2023, then fell to zero among identified post-wave jumbo transfers — at most about 4 per cent once unidentified deals are capped by theinsurer’s own disclosed premiums — while their share of small deals, where class-action exposure is negligible, was unchanged: a 52 percentage-point differential decline. The decline is significant on an exact test of the litigated cell that does not inherit the randomization design’s floor — twenty of thirty-eight large pre-wave transfers against none of eight after, p = 0.006 — while the control cell does not move (p = 0.83). Litigation, whether operating through fiduciary demand or insurer retreat, disciplines chain risk exactly where liability exposure is large, and leaves smaller plans’ transfers unpoliced — the boundary that defines the residual case for supervisory rather than litigation discipline.

detail.abstract: This study examines the ecological dynamics of the ongoing crisis in Gaza through the lens of "green apartheid," a concept denoting the systematic use of environmental access and natural assets as instruments of domination. Deforestation, water scarcity, agricultural devastation, and energy deprivation in Gaza are analysed not as incidental consequences of conflict but as deliberate mechanisms of political control. Drawing on Rob Nixon's theory of slow violence and postcolonial ecocriticism, this paper interprets Gaza's environmental condition as an ongoing, cumulative, and structurally invisible form of domination. The destruction of greenery and agriculture is shown to exceed material damage, severely affecting both survival and cultural identity. This analysis exposes how green apartheid constitutes a form of environmental segregation that restricts equitable access to ecological resources, positioning Gaza at the intersection of human survival and environmental justice. The study argues that Gaza's ecological crisis demonstrates how environment, politics, and culture intersect within colonial and postcolonial contexts. Recognising Gaza through a postcolonial framework reveals that environmental justice must account for both ecological conservation and cultural survival, ensuring the balance of human and non-human existence. This qualitative document analysis offers fresh opportunities to explore how examining ecological oppression through a postcolonial lens can reshape understandings of environmental justice and resistance.

title: Alignment through Interdependence: Global Value Chains and Geopolitical Swing States

detail.title: Alignment through Interdependence: Global Value Chains and Geopolitical Swing States

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: I gratefully acknowledge financial support from the Niehaus Center for Globalization and Governance (NCGG).

detail.abstract: When does economic interdependence produce political alignment? I revisit this classical debate, and argue that manufacturing global value chains (GVCs), more than resource or market ties, draw geopolitical swing states toward the major powers whose firms anchor those chains. GVC integration advances core developmental goals of export promotion and industrial upgrading, and specialized production relationships are costly to replace. Host governments therefore protect these ties by signaling political alignment that reassures existing and future investors. Globally, across partner-major-power dyads from 2004 to 2022, only co-production ties predict closer UN voting alignment, conditional on total trade. To identify causal effect, I exploit the reorganization of Chinese production after the 2018 U.S. tariff shock as a quasiexperimental test. I combine project-level data on Chinese greenfield investment with original text-based measures of alignment from leader visits and joint statements. A shift-share design shows that market-driven, GVC-integrating investment increases alignment with Beijing: host governments upgrade partnerships, sign strategic agreements, and endorse Chinese diplomatic priorities. The findings reveal how unilateral decoupling backfires in the GVC era: tariffs meant to weaken a rival could inadvertently extend and deepen its production networks and political influence into third countries.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates price adjustment speed, price discovery, and conditional volatility dynamics across the Brazilian interest rate term structure following US macroeconomic announcements (Non-Farm Payroll and CPI). Using 1-minute high-frequency data of Brazilian DI futures contracts traded on B3 across three maturities-short (DI1F29), intermediate (DI1F32), and long (DI1F37)-, we conduct an intraday event study and estimate joint AR(1)-GARCH(1,1)-X models with HAC Newey-West robust standard errors. Empirical findings reveal monotonic term-structure heterogeneity: in the conditional mean equation, the directional impact of exogenous surprises peaks at the short end and decreases monotonically toward the long end (β Pay declines from +0.3884 to +0.2241; β CPI decreases from +0.2874 to +0.1362, both statistically significant). In the conditional variance equation, releases trigger immediate volatility spikes (γ ≈ 0.046 to 0.049), while persistence (α + β) increases with contractual maturity (0.9257 for DI1F29, 0.9635 for DI1F32, and 0.9812 for DI1F37). The findings support the semi-strong form of the Efficient Market Hypothesis and show that international shocks primarily alter short-to-medium-term domestic monetary policy expectations, whereas longer maturities experience prolonged volatility clustering.

Evidence-concordance Governance for Fracture Imaging AI 
A Methodological Internal-validation Study of Diagnostic, Spatial, Geometric and Integrity Evidence
