detail.abstract: Medical imaging AI can generate accurate predictions while still failing to establish that a high-confidence output is anatomically coherent, spatially supported, morphologically plausible, stable, or within a validated operating domain. We propose an evidence-concordance governance framework in which acceptance is based on independently derived evidence rather than diagnostic confidence alone. The framework combines hierarchical clinical grounding, independently trained target detection and segmentation, ensemble stability, image integrity, and a separate geometric-conformity channel based on regional fractal and topological descriptors (RTFD/TDA) with split-conformal Mahalanobis calibration. On FracAtlas, 4,024 valid radiographs were available, including 717 fracture-positive images. A ResNet50-based fracture classifier achieved AUROC 0.8901 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.855-0.924) and average precision 0.7324 (0.655-0.806) on a 604-image internal test cohort. Anatomical classification reached 95.70% accuracy and 84.39% balanced accuracy. A separately trained YOLO26s detector achieved mean best-box IoU 0.4848 (0.424-0.545) and IoU>=0.50 recall 59.26%; YOLO26s-seg achieved mean mask IoU 0.3890 (0.338-0.440). The primary soft Evidence Concordance Score (ECS), based on diagnostic certainty, target agreement, segmentation agreement and ensemble stability, used a calibration-selected threshold of 0.9154 and accepted 177/604 test cases (29.3%) with 0 observed errors. A conjunctive sensitivity analysis using the minimum of the four evidence components selected 200/604 cases (33.1%) with 1 observed error (0.50%). At the same 177-case coverage, diagnostic-confidence-only selection produced 3 errors (1.69%). A simple confidence-plus-ensemble-stability comparator had 5 errors at the 33.1% conjunctive operating point. The exact 95% upper bound for 0/177 accepted-case errors was 2.1%. RTFD/TDA was retained as a separate geometric-conformity channel rather than folded into ECS. These findings support evidence-concordant selective acceptance as a methodological governance strategy for fracture imaging. The study is an internal, single-dataset validation; the development programme was iterative across multiple experimental versions, so the current test cohort should not be interpreted as an untouched confirmatory estimate. The study does not establish patient-level independence, external generalization, or clinical safety. Relationship to prior work. Our earlier 2025 study introduced TDA and fractal features from CNN representations for interpretable, robust and OOD-aware medical-image analysis [1]. The present study preserves that geometric foundation while upgrading the objective from feature-level explanation toward case-level evidence governance. Key message: trust is treated as a testable property of concordance among independent evidence streams, not as a synonym for model confidence.

detail.abstract: Contemporary educational administration faces the tension between the "chief administrator" model-a legacy of Weberian bureaucratic rationality-and the growing demand for distributed and participatory forms of leadership capable of sustaining learning in contexts of high uncertainty. This theoretical article examines teamwork as a situated form of governance, in which distributed leadership, the micropolitics of power, conflict transformation, and reflective practice operate as interdependent dimensions of the same organizational dynamic. Based on a literature review of the Educational Administration seminar-executive leadership (Murillo Torrecilla, 2020), strategic planning (Tedesco, 2019), reengineering (Aguerrondo, 2018), educational governance (Guzmán-Valenzuela, 2019; UNESCO/OREALC, 2021), school micropolitics (Peniche Cetzal et al., 2012), and conflict transformation (Pérez-Archundia and Gutiérrez-Méndez, 2016)-and by comparing two illustrative cases, one institutional (a rural school in Quindío, Colombia) and one community-based (the leadership of a social leader in the municipality of Quimbaya, Quindío)-1 Article based on work conducted during the Educational Administration Seminar, Doctor of Education program, University of the Americas and the Caribbean. 2 a conceptual model of Network-Based Educational Governance is proposed that integrates both levels. It follows from the above that effective teamwork cannot be attributed to the individual qualities of a leader. Rather, it arises from the way power is distributed and from a contextualized interpretation of norms, supported by an institution (whether the school or its community environment) willing to view conflict as the foundation for learning.

detail.abstract: We study the quadratic tracking problem of a general stochastic target process with absolutely continuous controls, with and without terminal constraint. We derive explicit, non-asymptotic upper bounds in terms of a Besov-type modulus of the target. These bounds yield sharp explicit rates that specialize to the square-root order for semimartingale targets. We then apply these results to a generalized Obizhaeva–Wang execution model with random terminal inventory. We first develop a Hilbert-space approach to characterize its optimal strategy, which includes jumps. To avoid such trading spikes, one regularizes the problem by a quadratic trading-rate penalty with coefficient ε. We then show that the regularized optimal execution cost—and therefore the excess price impact cost of the regularized optimal strategy—converges at the sharp rate O(√ ε). Since the regularized optimal strategy is not available in closed form, we further construct a nearly optimal strategy which is readily implementable and shares the same approximation rate.

detail.abstract:
Bessembinder (2018) documented that the top four percent of US listed firms created all net stock market wealth from 1926 to 2016, concluding the only way to hold the winners is to hold everything. Whether Bessembinder capture can be operationalised systematically is an open question: the closest prior attempt (Erstad and Lorentzen, 2021) concluded that quality-based screening lacks predictive power on wealth-generating stocks at monthly horizons.
This paper proposes a four-stage framework applied at eight distress episodes across
2007–2024: stability selection under hierarchical Dirichlet resampling with Benjamini-
Hochberg FDR control, Ward clustering with core-satellite sizing, and an empirical
Bayes Beta-Binomial prior on per-stock binary re-selection indicators.
The backtest retains 88.3 percent of Bessembinder top-4 percent dollar wealth by
holding 35.8 percent of the eligible universe: a 2.46× concentration-efficiency ra-
tio (Fisher exact p ≈ 2 × 10−5). A 42-month live deployment via a verified broker
account confirms 86.7 percent capture by holding 6.6 percent of the out-of-sample
universe: a 13.1× ratio, with the top five wealth creators held in full. Framework re-
turns decompose to factor exposure with no residual alpha, consistent with the non-
arbitrage frame under which the paper operates.
Three contributions follow. This is the first forward-looking systematic framework in
the academic literature for prospective wealth-creator capture; the empirical Bayes
prior on per-stock binary re-selection indicators has no direct precedent in portfolio
construction; and the broker-timestamped live-execution record extends the Bessembinder-
derivative literature beyond backtest evidence. The mechanism is persistence: for
four percent of firms to dominate century-scale wealth creation, top-percentile mem-
bership must persist across measurement windows, and price-derived stability sig-
nals resolve this persistence directly.

detail.abstract: Quantitative trading usually judges a strategy by the light it has already emitted: its past performance. But a record of yesterday's returns cannot tell us whether the signal producing them remains structurally alive today, or how long it has left. This paper develops SAGE, a Signal Autopsy Graph Engine that reframes strategy evaluation as a survival problem. Using ten trading-signal families and a decade of daily ETF data, SAGE defines death through forward, after-cost performance; predicts that death from strictly backward-looking health features; and uses crowding and counterfactual signal twins to distinguish among possible causes of decay. On data never seen during fitting, from July 2021 through December 2024, a logistic model predicts death 63 trading days ahead with an AUC of 0.573 (95% bootstrap CI [0.561, 0.586]; permutation p = 0.0005), while a Cox proportional-hazards model reaches a concordance of 0.550. Walk-forward validation across five successive windows shows that the result is not trapped inside one lucky split: four of five folds lie above chance, and the skill strengthens in recent years. Crowding, measured as a signal's rolling correlation with its peers, emerges as one of the strongest predictors of death, giving direct empirical support to the claim that signals die inside crowded families. The out-ofsample allocation period offered no profitable long exposure, and every method lost money. Even there, however, the dollar-neutral SAGE book that shorted predicted-dead signals produced the best riskadjusted result of five methods, while naive performance chasing produced the worst. The central finding is therefore modest but real. Alpha decay is predictable out of sample, and the prediction creates relative value even in a period when absolute returns remain negative.

detail.abstract: Existing literature is unsettled regarding whether close lending relationships are beneficial or detrimental to borrowers. Using bank-merger events as a shock to debt concentration, we find that positive shocks to concentration result in decreased borrower credit, investment, and growth. Lenders reduce lending most to borrowers that are reliant upon them. This is evidence of lenders taking advantage of higher switching costs and reduced borrower bargaining power to exploit borrowers. Our findings suggest substantial costs of concentrated relationships.

title: Beyond Criticality: Testing Hierarchical Genesis in Adaptive Networks

detail.abstract:
Hierarchical Genesis Theory (HGT) proposes that a critical transition alone is insufficient to establish the formation of a new organizational level. The Hierarchical Genesis Condition (HGC) therefore requires five operational properties: structural destabilization (H1), persistent collective-variable formation (H2), functional integration (H3), higher-to-lower constraint (H4), and relative dynamical autonomy (H5). This study tests whether HGC can discriminate candidate hierarchical genesis from criticality alone in a 24-component stochastic adaptive network under finite capacity. Two matched systems share identical critical-mode dynamics, collective-variable persistence, hysteresis, and macro-level predictive autonomy while differing in higher-to-lower coupling. In a representative realization, the coupled system yields normalized q-associated integration I~q=0.1863\widetilde{I}_q = 0.1863 and a standardized intervention effect Eq→X=0.2085E_{q\to X} = 0.2085, whereas the uncoupled control yields I~q=0.00061\widetilde{I}_q = 0.00061 and Eq→X=0E_{q\to X} = 0.

Because this binary comparison is structurally strong, coupling is then varied continuously as bi=γbi(0)b_i=\gamma b_i^{(0)} over 0≤γ≤1.20\leq\gamma\leq1.2. Across eight stochastic replicates, H4 increases approximately monotonically with coupling, whereas H3 remains near zero under weak coupling and rises nonlinearly at stronger coupling. Under the illustrative HGT-I decision criteria I~q≥0.10\widetilde{I}_q\geq0.10 and Eq→X≥0.20E_{q\to X}\geq0.20, both mean measures first enter the candidate-positive region near γ=1.0\gamma=1.0. The result does not identify a universal phase transition. Rather, it supports the central HGT distinction that a critical transition is not equivalent to hierarchical genesis. HGC can operationally distinguish criticality and persistent macrodynamics from a stronger regime in which an emergent collective variable becomes both integrative and dynamically consequential for its constituents. The study therefore extends HGT from a proof of dynamical possibility to a computational demonstration of discrimination in a high-dimensional adaptive network.

title: The Same Career, a Different Margin

detail.title: The Same Career, a Different Margin

detail.abstract: This paper compares the financial position of a mid-career professional — Engineer III — in 1976 and 2026, using U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics salary data, Consumer Price Index deflators, Census and HUD housing figures, Freddie Mac mortgage rates, IRS tax rules, and KFF health-insurance benchmarks. The 2026 Aerospace Engineer III earns approximately 7 percent more in real, CPI-adjusted terms than the 1976 Engineer III, and faces a lower combined federal income and payroll tax burden as a share of salary. Real wage growth alone would suggest an improved financial position. A household-level model incorporating housing costs, mortgage terms, employee health-insurance contributions, and education debt shows the opposite: median new-home price relative to salary rose from roughly 2.5x to 3.6x, the income share required for a 20 percent down payment rose from about half a year's salary to over 70 percent, and modern employee-side health and education costs consume income unavailable to the 1976 household. Net household margin — income remaining after these major costs — is flat to modestly lower in 2026 despite the real wage gain. The paper argues that CPI-based wage comparisons and household financial-margin analysis answer different questions, and that rising nominal and even real wages can coexist with declining capacity to build middle-class assets. Findings are illustrative of a specific occupation and household structure rather than national disposable-income statistics.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how inflation spillovers in Peru vary across the joint distribution of paired inflation components and across time horizons, using a quantile-on-quantile connectedness framework applied to two complementary partitions of the CPI basket: Core versus Non-Core, capturing the persistence dimension of price shocks, and Tradable versus Non-Tradable, capturing their exposure to international markets. We estimate spillovers at each pair of quantiles rather than at the conditional mean, further decomposing connectedness into short-run and long-run frequency bands to separate transitory from persistent transmission. We find that transmission is neither linear nor fixed, but depends jointly on the quantile pair and the frequency band considered: connectedness at the conditional mean substantially understates tail dependence, reaching several times the mean-based estimate when both series share the same tail. More strikingly, the direction of transmission reverses across the frequency spectrum-the conventional second-round effect (Non-Core to Core, Tradable to Non-Tradable) dominates at short-run frequencies but reverses at longer horizons, with Core and Non-Tradable becoming the net transmitters instead. This double dependence, masked entirely by conditional-mean estimates, indicates that these transmission mechanisms are considerably more state-and horizon-dependent than previously recognized.

detail.abstract:
This report explores the problems posed by the affordable housing crisis in India and
seeks to integrate a technological solution in AI to mitigate the conundrum. The paper studies

detail.abstract: Oil, gas, and water pipelines stretch out across thousands of kilometers. Any number of minor issues could turn into major problems, such as leaks or explosions, or force an interruption of operations. Existing inspection processes still involve manual human inspection, checking pressure gauges, and watching hours upon hours of CCTV footage for any defects or signs of defects that need further investigation. The current paper proposes a deep learning object detection-based pipeline inspection system utilizing YOLOv8 to automatically detect defects in the pipeline. The defects appear as bounding boxes in the output, but rather than stopping there, the second module takes the detection output and analyzes it in relation to the company's internal maintenance knowledge base using large language models. The result is a description of the detected defect, potential repairs required, estimated urgency level of the repair, and an optimal method for completing that repair. The overall system translates camera inputs into tangible maintenance tickets. The paper outlines both the architecture of the proposed solution, as well as its data preprocessing and annotation steps, model training methodology, and fix suggestion process. It also includes relevant performance metrics, strengths and weaknesses, and suggestions for further work in this space. The aim of the paper is to present an overview of this idea that is comprehensible to readers unfamiliar with computer vision, as well as those who work directly in pipeline inspection.

title:

detail.abstract:
This report builds a Systemic Ageing Index (SAI) for ten of the world's largest economies — the United States, China, Germany, Japan, the United Kingdom, India, France, Italy, Russia and Canada — using four published, independently verifiable indices: infrastructure quality (IMD World Competitiveness Center), government effectiveness (World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators), innovation capability (WIPO Global Innovation Index), and the pace of demographic change through 2040 (UN World Population Prospects).

The resulting ranking overturns a common intuition. Russia, Italy and India show the largest capability gaps in this sample — Russia and Italy because weak institutions and infrastructure combine with a fast-approaching demographic transition (Italy) or already-constrained state capacity (Russia); India because its infrastructure and innovation base still trails the global frontier by a wide margin, even though its demographic position is the most favourable of the ten. The United States, Japan and Canada show the smallest gaps — not because their infrastructure is new, but because strong institutions and technology capability offset whatever physical ageing exists, and in Japan's case, offset a demographic transition that is otherwise one of the most advanced in the world.

Against McKinsey's published estimate of $106 trillion in global infrastructure investment needed through 2040, this report does not attempt to invent a country-by-country or sector-by-sector breakdown beyond what McKinsey, the World Bank and the IEA have themselves published. It instead uses the real regional and sectoral splits already available — Asia's roughly two-thirds share of the global total, the persistent gap between global electricity generation and grid investment reported by the IEA, and the $200 billion record year for private infrastructure fundraising reported by McKinsey — to frame where capital is most needed and where it is currently most constrained.

The report closes with a set of recommendations organised around a simple, defensible principle: renewal investment should be prioritised by the size of the measured capability gap and the criticality of the system in question, not by the age of the asset or the visibility of the project. Where this report cannot support a specific number with real data, it says so plainly rather than filling the gap with an invented one.

title: From Transit to Control: Chinese Equipment by Rail to Central Asia

detail.title: From Transit to Control: Chinese Equipment by Rail to Central Asia

detail.abstract: The familiar description of China-Central Asia rail trade as transit conceals the transaction that produces the greatest legal change. Chinese equipment may reach Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, or the Kyrgyz Republic by rail and then stop. It enters a logistics center, dry port, bonded warehouse, free customs zone, industrial site, or assembly facility. Components are stored, tested, configured, packaged, repaired, combined, or released to a buyer whose identity may not have been known when the train left China. This article treats that stop as a distinct legal event. It argues that regional value is created only when the physical operation is matched by an auditable chain of carriage, custody, customs status, technical work, origin, end use, and resale. Postponement theory explains the commercial reason for delayed configuration. It does not establish origin or defeat export controls. Rail documentation facilitates movement but cannot prove later manufacturing, warehouse authority, or lawful destination. The proposed model therefore replaces the loose idea of a transit corridor with a legal architecture of controlled value addition. Its central instrument is a continuously maintained assembly compliance file linking the Chinese supplier, carrier, border transfer, warehouse, contractor, customs declaration, and final sale. Central Asia can become a regional platform for equipment distribution and technical services, but the model fails when storage is presented as production, simple assembly is presented as substantial transformation, or a free customs zone is treated as a device for erasing destination risk.

title: The Self-preservation Relay and Risk Amplification Loop: How Locally Rational Defensive Actions Escalate Organizational Conflict

detail.abstract:
This paper proposes the concept of the Self-Preservation Relay to explain why organizations confronted with problem-raising, whistleblowing, harassment complaints, criticism of managers, or workplace improvement proposals may move not toward substantive inquiry, dialogue, and repair, but toward silence, distancing, proceduralization, written apologies, reflections, transfers, the search for disciplinary grounds, and the transformation of the problem-raiser into a management object. The Self-Preservation Relay refers to a process in which multiple organizational actors choose locally rational defensive actions to protect their evaluation, responsibility, role, prior decisions, professional self-image, interpersonal relations, workplace operation, face, or institutional legitimacy, and in which these actions become the decision environment for other actors. Through this relay, silence, responsibility avoidance, formalization, justification, distancing, the search for sanctionable grounds, and the problematization of the problem-raiser are reproduced across actors.

The paper does not treat self-preservation as inherently immoral. Self-preservation is an almost unavoidable feature of organizational life. The central issue is whether it is opened toward accountability, fact-finding, third-party verification, retrospective examination, and relational repair, or closed toward silence, procedural control, defense of prior judgments, and the management of the problem-raiser. Drawing on research on bounded rationality, organizational defensive routines, psychological safety, organizational silence, threat-rigidity, institutional legitimacy, whistleblower retaliation, and procedural justice, the paper positions the Self-Preservation Relay as a middle-range theoretical concept.

The paper develops an analytical vignette to show how locally rational judgments by a local manager, a senior branch manager, and an upper-level manager may become connected. The vignette illustrates how the organizational focus can shift from examining what happened to managing and distancing the problem-raiser. Within this process, the paper introduces three auxiliary concepts: pretext-seeking observation, defensive incorporation, and forward-only remediation. It then argues that the Self-Preservation Relay may begin as short-term risk reduction but turn into a Risk Amplification Loop, increasing legal risk, reputational risk, internal trust risk, and the deterioration of organizational learning capacity.

title: The Transparency Penalty: Voluntary Self-correction, Common-source Amplification, and the Porandla Case
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: The Transparency Penalty: Voluntary Self-correction, Common-source Amplification, and the Porandla Case

declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this article.

detail.abstract: Researchers are repeatedly told that identifying and correcting their own errors is the responsible course of action. Yet the public consequences of voluntary correction are not determined by the retraction notice alone. This documentary case study examines what happened after Rishika Porandla notified Wiley about a paper based on work undertaken while she was in high school, agreed to its retraction, and later approached Retraction Watch to discuss the experience. The study reconstructs the public record from the retraction notice of 22 May 2026 through 25 August 2026 and distinguishes five analytically separate processes: correction of the literature, scientific scrutiny, expansion into adjacent publications and personal activities, repetition of a common source across identities and platforms, and durable reputational amplification. The chronology shows that an initially affirmative Retraction Watch story published on 10 August became the discovery surface for PubPeer comments, additions to the story, further discussion of unrelated or partly related work, a second Retraction Watch article on 14 August, treatment by For Better Science on the same day, syndication by The Scientist, and inclusion in a paid Retraction Watch newsletter. A particularly important finding is that Kevin Patrick was publicly identified by Retraction Watch as using both “Actinopolyspora biskrensis” and “Cheshire.” In the case record, those identities appeared respectively as a PubPeer commenter, a Retraction Watch commenter directing readers to PubPeer, and a named source in the follow-up article. Multiple visible signals therefore did not always represent independent evidentiary sources. The Retraction Watch comment sections also retained personal, speculative, and sanction-oriented statements that appear difficult to reconcile with the outlet’s published rule against ad hominem attacks, unverified facts, and speculation about motive. The case does not establish secret coordination, donor influence, paid targeting, or the truth or falsity of every scientific concern. It establishes something more readily demonstrable: functional convergence, common-source amplification, scope expansion, and moderation inconsistency. The article concludes that “watchdog” authority must not be treated as a self-conferred credential. Where source independence, role disclosure, proportionality, moderation, and correction symmetry are not auditable, institutions and readers should withhold that status and treat platform visibility as a lead requiring independent verification rather than as adjudicated authority.

title: Routing through Traffic Signals: The Value, Depth, and Accuracy of Phase Information

detail.title: Routing through Traffic Signals: The Value, Depth, and Accuracy of Phase Information

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: Problem definition: Navigation systems choose routes by representing traffic signals as static average turn penalties, while real-time phase information available at production scale is used for display and speed advisory. We ask how much realized, movement-level phase information is worth to a router facing fixed-time signals, how this value depends on its depth and accuracy, and what the optimal rule looks like at each information level. Methodology/results: We study a movement-expanded network with per-movement residual waits, uncontrolled right turns, and configurable per-axis phase plans. Our analysis combines shortest-path arguments, coupling, and stochastic shortest-path theory with grid experiments and microscopic simulation. Cruising at the speed cap and waiting at stoplines is time-optimal on every route, so the optimal arrival-time frontier is attained by route choice alone. The myopic take-the-green rule can perform worse than static routing by a factor of order the cycle length over the sum of the shortest link and crossing times. In expectation, it outperforms static routing only below an explicit link-heterogeneity threshold governed by the Gini mean difference of link times. Timing error costs at most the error itself while planned and realized timelines remain synchronized, with red phases acting to resynchronize them; empirically, timing information breaks even near a quarter cycle of error. Rolling lookahead admits explicit regret guarantees and closes the optimality gap near-geometrically. When offsets are unknown, the optimal always-advancing policy is a link-stationary threshold rule, and its value shows that observing the light ahead closes about one third of the static-to-full-information gap. Implications: A deployable countdown-based threshold rule captures a substantial share of the value of full timing information. The results quantify how information providers should price depth against accuracy. Under congestion, queue-ignorant deep timing plans lose their advantage, whereas the shallow rule remains robust, including against a traffic-aware baseline.

detail.abstract: Semiconductor capital allocation is commonly represented as a financial decision applied to a technical program. That sequence obscures an important dependency: architecture can constrain much of the capital decision before formal authorization occurs, while later implementation, manufacturing, commercial, and policy premises determine how much of that exposure actually crystallizes. Process node, die partitioning, memory hierarchy, package technology, verification scope, supplier set, qualification path, manufacturing geography, and capacity exposure can become financial assumptions as the acceptable implementation set narrows. This paper proposes a semiconductor-specific operating representation—an architecture-to-capital trace linking material premises to the commitments that depend on them, the go-forward value basis for each commitment, the ordinary financial-model term affected, the realistic operational/economic value recoverable if those premises fail, the evidence state of each premise, admissibility conditions, and accountable domain reviewers and capital decision authorities. It builds explicitly on design-to-cost, requirements traceability, risk management, engineering-change propagation, modularity, real-options, Stage-Gate, discovery-driven planning, integrated architecture-cost modeling, valuedriven systems engineering, and independent technical-authority practice rather than claiming those mechanisms are new. Public cases from Intel, NVIDIA, and CHIPS implementation show why the additional linkage can matter in semiconductors: node economics can depend on external volume; fabless architectures can create large supply obligations; a policy boundary can strand inventory and contractual commitments after a product is built; and sovereign capital can deliberately alter ordinary milestone conditions. An illustrative demonstrator then decomposes a prospective semiconductor commitment boundary, maps its components into the ordinary economic model—including incremental NRE, cash-flow or working-capital effects, contractual exposure, and expected loss where applicable—and shows how common-path work can proceed while premise-dependent irreversibility remains optional. It does so without replacing the substrate-selection, trust/admission, capital-structure, or expected-value decisions established in prior Living Cipher analyses and ordinary finance. The argument is not that engineers should replace finance. It is that capital diligence is incomplete when the technical and implementation premises that make the financial model possible are detached from their evidence state and from the domains accountable for validating that evidence.

title:
Human-AI Cognitive Co-evolution

From Cognitive Synergy to the Recursive Development of Human and Artificial Cognitive Capability

detail.title:
Human-AI Cognitive Co-evolution

From Cognitive Synergy to the Recursive Development of Human and Artificial Cognitive Capability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: Research on human-AI interaction has largely examined what humans and artificial intelligence can accomplish together. Studies increasingly document effects on productivity, task performance, decision making, learning, creativity, and professional work. A different question has received considerably less longitudinal attention: what does sustained interaction cause the participants and their cognitive relationship to become over time? This paper develops Human-AI Cognitive Co-evolution (HACC) as a theoretical framework for examining that question. HACC concerns the recursive developmental process through which sustained interaction between human and artificial cognition can alter human cognitive capabilities, the effective cognitive contribution obtainable from artificial intelligence, the relationship through which those capabilities are combined, and the resulting joint cognitive capability of the human-AI system. HACC extends the earlier Human-AI Cognitive Synergy formulation by shifting the unit of analysis from developmental effects principally on the human participant to reciprocal developmental dynamics within the human-AI relationship. Reciprocity does not imply symmetry. Humans develop through learning, experience, reflection, knowledge acquisition, strategy formation, neuroplastic adaptation, and changes in judgment. Artificial systems change through fundamentally different mechanisms, including model development, system configuration, context, memory, retrieval, tool integration, and changes in the capabilities that human users are able to elicit from otherwise unchanged systems. The framework distinguishes HACC from Human-AI Cognitive Outsourcing (HACO), a trajectory in which artificial intelligence performs an increasing share of cognitive activity without corresponding development of the human capabilities necessary to perform, understand, evaluate, or meaningfully integrate that activity. HACC and HACO are not binary states. Different cognitive capabilities may simultaneously be developed, maintained, deliberately delegated, or displaced. The paper further distinguishes local capability bounds, interaction bounds, and long-run developmental bounds. Particular human, artificial, and joint capabilities are constrained. Individual recursive episodes must also terminate when the expected value of further cognitive iteration no longer justifies its costs. These observations do not, however, establish that the developmental trajectory of a changing human-AI cognitive system must converge toward a single fixed global ceiling. HACC therefore treats long-run development as potentially open-ended rather than unbounded, leaving the existence and location of global developmental limits as empirical questions. A dynamic model is developed to represent multidimensional human capability, base and effective artificial capability, recursive interaction, cognitive complementarity, joint capability, cognitive outsourcing, endogenous local frontiers, regime change, problem-space expansion and contraction, and bounded recursive episodes. The framework generates falsifiable propositions and identifies the longitudinal evidence required to distinguish cognitive co-evolution from augmentation, learning, adaptation, and outsourcing. The central proposition is not that human-AI cognitive co-evolution has already been empirically demonstrated. It is that increasingly persistent interaction between human and artificial cognition creates developmental relationships that cannot be understood adequately through measures of immediate performance alone. Understanding those relationships requires examining not only what humans and AI produce together, but what capabilities they develop, preserve, reconfigure, or lose through sustained interaction.

title: When a Short Seller Becomes a Science Watchdog: Gotham City Research, Retraction Watch, and the Financial-Interest Gap in the Shinya Yamanaka Case
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: When a Short Seller Becomes a Science Watchdog: Gotham City Research, Retraction Watch, and the Financial-Interest Gap in the Shinya Yamanaka Case

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial, employment, institutional, or trading relationship with the organisations, companies, platforms, journals, or individuals discussed in this article.

detail.abstract: This article examines a documented collision between investment research and science-integrity journalism. A report issued by Gotham City Research LLC and General Industrial Partners LLP linked image-related concerns in a group of scientific papers to the commercial prospects of two Japanese companies and to the reputation of Shinya Yamanaka and the Center for iPS Cell Research and Application. The report disclosed a short position and the possibility that positions could be reduced after publication. It also relied substantially on pre-existing PubPeer comments and combined papers with materially different authorship roles, investigative histories, and editorial outcomes. Retraction Watch later reported the dispute, identified Gotham as a short seller, and included the institutional response, but did not publish an independent technical adjudication or a complete account of the report’s co-producer and conflict chain. The central concern is therefore not that financially interested actors must be excluded from raising scientific questions. It is that a disclosure of financial interest is only the beginning of scrutiny, not a substitute for verification. When allegations can produce both market and reputational effects, publishers must distinguish observation from misconduct, identify inherited evidence, test each paper separately, disclose all materially interested actors, obtain a meaningful response before publication, and provide correction and outcome tracking with equal prominence. The article proposes a financially interested source protocol for science journalism and post-publication platforms. It rejects unsupported claims of geopolitical coordination, funding bargains, or trading misconduct while demonstrating a serious and remediable governance gap.

detail.abstract:
Organizations often treat adaptation as a response to a changing environment. This paper asks a prior question. Why does the object of adaptation keep changing in the first place?
It proposes constraint migration as a mechanism. When a binding constraint is relieved, pressure does not disappear. It moves to another part of the system. The paper argues that organizational performance depends less on adaptation speed alone and more on adaptation speed relative to the rate at which the constraint landscape changes.
The paper develops this argument conceptually. It distinguishes the mechanism from the theory of constraints, dynamic capabilities, and OODA. It derives five testable propositions, including one that separates the framework from the simpler claim that faster-adapting firms just perform better regardless of context. Three cases illustrate the mechanism rather than test it, the AI accelerator supply chain from 2023 to 2026, takeaway capacity in the Bakken shale from 2010 to 2019, and COVID-19 vaccine manufacturing and distribution from 2020 to 2022. The framework is provisional. The propositions are hypotheses, not findings. The paper states the conditions under which the mechanism may fail.

detail.abstract: The current study sought to identify the impact of digital leadership on strategic success in Iraqi university institutions. The study was condusted in the colleges of Misan University, where a questionnaire was distributed to a sample of (97) managers, and (89) valid questionnaires were obtained for analysis. The study adopted the descriptive-analytical approach and relied on four dimensions of the independent variable, digital leadership. The study questions were answered through testing a number of hypotheses concerning variance, relationship, and impact using the statistical program (SPSS V.26). The study reached several conclusions, the most important of which is that the dimensions of digital leadership affect strategic success. The study also found a statistically significant correlation between digital leadership, with its dimensions, and strategic success. Furthermore, the results indicated a statistically significant impact of digital leadership, at both the overall level and the level of its dimensions, on strategic success. The study also found variation in the impact of the dimensions of digital leadership on strategic success in the universities under study. The study presented several recommendations to the management of the university under study, the most important of which is the need to deepen attention to digital leadership because of its importance in developing and achieving the objectives of the university institution at the strategic level.

title: Newborn Screening at Scale

detail.title: Newborn Screening at Scale

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This paper is the independent work of the author. detail.abstract:
Background. Sickle cell disease is a major contributor to avoidable child mortality in sub-Saharan Africa. The Global Burden of Disease Study 2021 attributes 81,100 deaths in children under five to the condition and estimates 376,000 total deaths when excess mortality is included, nearly eleven times the number captured through cause-specific coding alone (GBD 2021 Sickle Cell Disease Collaborators, 2023). In Nigeria, modelling of the 2018 Demographic and Health Survey estimates under-five mortality among affected children at approximately 490 per 1,000 livebirths and attributes about 4.2% of national under-five deaths to excess sickle cell mortality (Nnodu et al., 2021). Most deaths can be prevented through established interventions, including early identification, penicillin prophylaxis, pneumococcal vaccination, parental education and structured follow-up. The challenge is therefore not identifying effective interventions, but delivering them at national scale.

Purpose. This paper proposes a phased implementation model for transitioning newborn screening for sickle cell disease from demonstration projects to national coverage. It is a design paper, not an evaluation. Its central premise is that screening should be treated not as a laboratory service seeking a delivery channel, but as a payload attached to an existing delivery platform with high national coverage.

Approach. The model draws on four evidence streams: cost-effectiveness literature on screening and prophylaxis in sub-Saharan Africa; operational experience from established African screening programmes in Ghana, Uganda, Angola and Tanzania; feasibility evidence on integrating screening into Nigerian immunisation contacts; and the programme architecture of long-running national screening systems, particularly the NHS Sickle Cell and Thalassaemia Screening Programme in England, used for transferable structural lessons rather than wholesale adoption.

Findings. Three design conclusions emerge. First, the principal constraint is not test cost but result-return logistics. Uganda's national programme achieved a cost of US$4.46 per test but a median inbound turnaround time of 16 days; a result received after families have dispersed is effectively a result not delivered (Hernandez et al., 2021). Second, point-of-care immunoassay testing at immunisation contacts can restructure this problem by converting specimen transport into a same-visit clinical encounter. Nigerian feasibility work reported 86% acceptability among mothers attending immunisation clinics (Oluwole et al., 2020). Third, national coverage is more realistically achieved through geographic phasing based on trait prevalence and primary-care readiness than through simultaneous nationwide implementation.

Contribution. The paper proposes a four-phase, eight-year implementation model with defined entry and exit criteria, a costed staffing and consumables envelope, a minimum indicator set, an explicit register of failure modes and mitigations, and a readiness instrument for state-level adoption. It argues that Nigeria's existing National Guideline already provides the core programme architecture; the principal deficit lies in implementation design, financing and accountability rather than policy intent (Federal Ministry of Health, 2022).

detail.abstract: Using California's SB 826 as a quasi-natural experiment, we find that a plausibly exogenous increase in board gender diversity lowers the CEO-to-employee pay ratio, apparently through lower CEO compensation rather than median employee pay. The reduction is stronger when female directors join the compensation committee. Tests do not support monitoring or stakeholder/reputation management, making an equity-preference explanation most consistent with the evidence. Large-language-model scoring of proxy-statement passages provides complementary evidence: gender diversity does not increase reactive, action-based language, while compensation-philosophy language is preserved among firms with greater female compensation-committee engagement but declines among firms with lower engagement.

title: CAT: An LLM-based Tool for Content Analysis in Experimental Economics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: We introduce the Communication Annotation Tool (CAT), an LLM-based tool for content analysis. CAT is intended to analyze free-form communication from economic experiments, accommodating a wide variety of communication structures. We describe CAT's features including a broad array of customization options and a template for developing a coding manual. A detailed guide for using CAT is provided, including a step-by-step demonstration showing how CAT is used to quantify the content of communication from an experimental dataset. CAT is designed for easy monitoring of the coding process which ensures replicability of the communication coding method and simplifies identification and resolution of problems. We conclude by discussing CAT's limitations and issues that users should keep in mind.

detail.abstract:
Background. Premarital genotype testing is widely practised in Nigeria and is, in some settings, effectively required by religious institutions, with churches in the south-east documented as refusing marriage on genotype grounds (Ugwu & Uneke, 2019). Community surveys indicate that most young adults consider genotype knowledge before marriage desirable, with around three quarters accepting screening (Isah et al., 2023). Yet Nigeria continues to record approximately 100,700 affected births annually (Nnodu et al., 2021). A practice that is widespread, socially endorsed and inexpensive is therefore not producing the outcome it is assumed to achieve.

Purpose. This paper asks why and specifies what a connected pathway would require. It advances a central structural claim: Nigeria has a widespread screening practice but no screening programme. The difference is not scale but connection—the presence of defined handoffs between testing, counselling, reproductive options, antenatal identification and postnatal care, with each step assigned an owner, time standard and measurable outcome.

Evidence. Comparative evidence comes from settings that have already tested different approaches. Saudi Arabia made premarital testing and counselling compulsory nationally; among 934 at-risk couples identified in 2005–2006, 824 (88.2%) married despite their risk status (Alswaidi et al., 2012; Memish & Saeedi, 2011). Cyprus, by contrast, reduced new births with thalassaemia major to near zero through a pathway in which certification was only the entry point, with prenatal diagnosis, cascade screening and lifelong clinical care connected to it (Cao et al., 2002; Cousens et al., 2010). The comparison suggests that mandating a test alone changes outcomes little; completing a connected pathway can change them substantially.

Findings. Four major disconnections are identified: testing without counselling, for which the workforce is inadequate at scale—the best-resourced health system on the continent has 28 genetic counsellors against a modelled requirement of 529 (Gomes et al., 2024); counselling without options, which reduces counselling to the delivery of bad news; results without records, leaving at-risk couples identified before marriage invisible to antenatal services years later; and disclosure without protection, which can turn a health intervention into a source of social harm.

Contribution. The paper proposes a five-stage pipeline with named owners, time standards and handoff
criteria; a tiered counselling model that places the bulk of the work with trained non-specialist cadres and
reserves scarce specialist capacity for complex cases; a consent-based at-risk couple register that carries
forward into antenatal care; and a set of safeguards intended to prevent the pathway from producing
discrimination. It closes with the conditions under which the model should be judged to have failed.

title: Reframing Data Privacy in the Era of Data Governance

detail.title: Reframing Data Privacy in the Era of Data Governance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no competing interests to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted as part of the author’s doctoral research at Copenhagen Business School (CBS). No external funding was received for this research

detail.abstract: SHORT PAPER. This article explores the evolving role of privacy within European data regulation, arguing that the traditional rights-based paradigm centred on individual autonomy is increasingly being reframed through the lens of a data governance approach. Rooted in the EU's fundamental rights tradition, the concept of privacy has historically functioned as a legal safeguard against the encroachment of public and private power, particularly through the protection of personal data. Yet contemporary regulatory developments-from the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) to the Data Act and Digital Markets Act-reflect a shift from privacy as an individual entitlement to privacy as a systemic governance concern. The analysis begins by tracing the normative origins of privacy, from its common law conception as the "right to be let alone" to its status as a foundational right underpinning democratic life. It then examines how privacy is operationalised within EU data protection law, highlighting tensions between normative aspirations and practical enforcement. As data becomes increasingly de-personalised, aggregated, or anonymised, traditional subject-centric models of privacy struggle to address the realities of automated processing and cross-border flows. In response, the article identifies a regulatory trend towards embedding privacy across the data lifecycle through organisational duties, stewardship mechanisms, and harmonised governance frameworks. This marks a movement away from post-hoc individual rights enforcement toward a standardsbased model that treats privacy as a principle to be structurally implemented. In doing so, EU law appears to be transitioning from protecting privacy to governing data-a shift with significant legal and conceptual implications.

title: Bounded Capacity Makes Substitutability Locally Testable

detail.title: Bounded Capacity Makes Substitutability Locally Testable

declarations.funderStatement: I used LLMs to assist with the preparation of this article, particularly GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5 (accessed in part via Poe with the support of Quora, where I am an advisor). This work was conducted while I was visiting the Technological Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Strategic Management (TIES) Group at the MIT Sloan School of Management; I greatly appreciate their hospitality.

detail.abstract: We study exact choice-oracle testing of substitutability in the setting of matching with contracts. Our first result sharpens the known exponential lower bound: At the identity choice function on n contracts, every substitutability certificate relative to the class of choice functions rationalized by strict preference orders over bundles and satisfying the law of aggregate demand must include the queries at all 2^n-2 nonempty proper menus. Hence, every randomized tester for the stated class with two-sided error at most ε makes at least (1-2ε)(2^n-2) expected queries at the identity choice function. By contrast, under irrelevance of rejected contracts and bounded capacity at most q, every failure of substitutability is witnessed on a menu of size at most q+2, which means that substitutability testing is polynomial in n for fixed q.

title: Financing Sickle Cell Disease Like it Matters

detail.title: Financing Sickle Cell Disease Like it Matters

It has not been submitted, in whole or in part, for the award of any qualification

detail.abstract:
Background. Sickle cell disease is a chronic condition with a largely predictable pattern of healthcare use, yet in Nigeria it is financed overwhelmingly through household out-of-pocket payments. Out-of-pocket spending accounts for roughly seven in every ten naira of current health expenditure (World Bank, 2025), while national health insurance enrolment stood at 21.7 million people in 2025 (Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, 2025), a small fraction of the population.

The measured burden. The consequences are substantial. Among 149 people with sickle cell disease attending a south-eastern tertiary institution, the median monthly economic burden was N76,711, reported by the authors as US$385, with outpatient costs accounting for approximately 88% (Amarachukwu et al., 2022). Catastrophic health expenditure was near-universal in the poorest quartile: 87.8% at the 10% threshold and 61.0% even at the 40% threshold. Among 314 Lagos parents of affected children, only 20.7% were enrolled in any health scheme and just 11.8% of those enrolled used it for payment; 95.5% of households relied on personal savings (Ogamba et al., 2020).

Argument. This paper argues that the financing failure is not primarily one of fiscal capacity but of specification. The instruments required already exist in Nigerian law. The National Health Act established the Basic Health Care Provision Fund, financed by not less than 1% of the Consolidated Revenue Fund (Federal Republic of Nigeria, 2014), while the National Health Insurance Authority Act made health insurance mandatory and requires every state to operate a scheme (Federal Republic of Nigeria, 2022). Sickle cell disease, however, is not defined within these instruments as a distinct benefit.

Contribution. The paper sets out why the condition is unusually well suited to prepayment; maps what each
existing instrument can and cannot fund; proposes a defined benefit package built around the
outpatient-dominant cost profile the evidence shows rather than the inpatient-dominant one the system
assumes; specifies a four-stage financing sequence; and proposes indicators that measure household financial
protection rather than enrolment counts.

title: Operational Performance Analysis of a Grid-Assisted Solar Photovoltaic–Battery Hybrid System at Wasso, Ngorongoro District, Tanzania
affiliations: Arusha Technical College and Arusha Technical College

detail.title: Operational Performance Analysis of a Grid-Assisted Solar Photovoltaic–Battery Hybrid System at Wasso, Ngorongoro District, Tanzania
detail.abstract: This paper analyses a grid-assisted solar photovoltaic (PV)–lithium iron phosphate battery hybrid system at Wasso, Tanzania (altitude ≈ 1 900 m), combining one week of five-minute telemetry (1 605 samples over 174.5 hours) with a six-month record of daily energy statistics (166 operational days, January–July 2026). Energy flows come from numerical integration, cross-validated against the platform's daily statistics. During the intensive week the array generated 382.9 kWh against a load of 739.5 kWh, with 374.6 kWh imported and none exported; direct PV, battery discharge and grid import met 40.6, 16.5 and 42.7 per cent of demand. Because the battery is also float-charged from the grid, at most 51 per cent of the load is of solar origin, close to the net-import self-sufficiency of 49.3 per cent; PV self-consumption is 100 per cent. Usable capacity, estimated coulometrically, is 21.1 kWh, cycled daily to a 24–26 per cent state-of-charge floor at about 75 per cent depth of discharge. The load shows a 16.6 kW peak, a 5.11 kW mean, a 30.8 per cent load factor and a persistent overnight base served by the grid. The six-month record corroborates the week: the net-import renewable fraction is 51.6 per cent, the capacity factor 14.7 per cent over all operational days and 16.8 per cent in service, and the seasonal renewable fraction 47 to 64 per cent. Storage capacity, not PV generation, is the binding constraint on clear days; recommendations for battery augmentation and load management are quantified

title: On the Joint Distribution of a Quadratic and a Linear Form in Normal Random Variables
affiliations: University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management, Stockholm University and Örebro University

detail.title: On the Joint Distribution of a Quadratic and a Linear Form in Normal Random Variables

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: We derive computable representations of the joint density and the joint cumulative distribution function of a quadratic form U = x ′Ax and a linear form V = a ′x when x has a multivariate normal distribution with arbitrary mean vector and nonsingular covariance matrix. In contrast to the double Laguerre series expansion of Schöne and Schmid (2000), which requires a zero mean vector and a positive semidenite A with rank greater than two, our results allow for a nonzero mean and an indenite A, and they impose no rank condition; the singular case A ∝ aa′ is characterized and solved in closed form, and the explicit critical curve on which the joint density can be unbounded is identied. Our main representation expresses the joint distribution function as a single integral of elementary functions involving the error function with complex argument, which can be evaluated quickly and to high accuracy by numerical quadrature. Two alternative representations, one based on conditioning and one based on an innite mixture of chi-squared distributions, provide independent verication. We further obtain, under explicit nondegeneracy conditions, the joint density of two quadratic forms and a linear form and the joint density of two general second-degree polynomials in normal random variables, and simple closed-form expressions for the conditional cumulant generating function and its derivatives of all orders, which deliver an integration-free saddlepoint approximation to the joint density at any chosen order of the (asymptotic) Daniels expansion. In numerical experiments, our single-integral formula reproduces Table I of Schöne and Schmid (2000) to within the accuracy of their reported values, with the entire table computed in a fraction of a second.

title: Making Hydroxyurea Boring: Converting a Proven Generic into Routine Sickle Cell Care

detail.title: Making Hydroxyurea Boring: Converting a Proven Generic into Routine Sickle Cell Care

detail.abstract:
Background. Hydroxyurea has been shown to reduce painful crises in sickle cell anaemia since a randomised trial was stopped early for benefit three decades ago (Charache et al., 1995), while long-term follow-up associated its use with reduced mortality (Steinberg et al., 2010). Concerns that these findings might not apply in malaria-endemic Africa were tested directly and were not supported: among 606 children across four African countries, treatment was associated with substantial reductions in sickle cell events, transfusion, malaria and death (Tshilolo et al., 2019). Extended follow-up over 4,340 patient-years confirmed these benefits without excess toxicity (Aygun et al., 2024).

The problem. Nigeria has the world's largest sickle cell burden, with approximately 100,700 affected births annually (Nnodu et al., 2021), and manufactures hydroxyurea domestically. Yet a national survey found that only 48.5% of surveyed patients had ever used it. Among prescribers, the leading barrier was perceived side effects (67.1%), rather than cost (Okocha et al., 2022). The gap between evidence and treatment is therefore not primarily one of evidence, price or regulatory status.

Argument. This paper argues that hydroxyurea in Nigeria is administered as though it were a specialist cytotoxic agent when it should be treated as an essential chronic medicine. Four structural barriers are identified: monitoring requirements disproportionate to observed toxicity; inadequate prescriber confidence reinforced by the absence of an authoritative protocol; supply chains without a dedicated budget line; and measurement systems that count prescriptions rather than sustained treatment.

Contribution. The paper proposes a three-tier delivery model that shifts continuation and refills to primary care while reserving complex initiation for specialist centres; two dosing protocols matched to laboratory capacity, including a simplified regimen supported by recent Nigerian operational evidence (Nri-Ezedi et al., 2025); a monitoring schedule calibrated to observed dose-limiting toxicity rather than inherited caution; a financing sequence informed by Ghana's inclusion of hydroxyurea in a national benefit package (Ofori-Acquah et al., 2023; Segbefia et al., 2025); and indicators focused on treatment retention rather than prescriptions written.

title: The Sundiata Post Model: Journalism as a Knowledge Institution — Architecture, Endurance, and Legacy

detail.title: The Sundiata Post Model: Journalism as a Knowledge Institution — Architecture, Endurance, and Legacy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder and Chief Executive Officer, Sundiata Post Media Ltd. and Lead Researcher, Sundiata Post Intelligence Unit (SPIU), the institution whose model is described in this paper. This relationship is disclosed transparently to ensure full academic integrity. No external funding was received for the development of this paper. The author has no financial or personal relationships with any other individuals or organisations that could inappropriately influence or bias the work presented here.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces and formally defines the Sundiata Post Model (SPM), an institutional model for media-based knowledge production in which an independent newsroom systematically integrates journalism, original research, conceptual innovation, and scholarly dissemination to produce original analytical constructs that contribute to public understanding, academic inquiry, and policy discourse within the global knowledge ecosystem. Developed from the operational experience of the Sundiata Post, an independent Nigerian newsroom, and first articulated across a seven-part series in its weekly column, ‘The Sunday Stew’, the Model proposes a Dual Engine Architecture in which a Media Operations Engine and a Knowledge Operations Engine function as mutually reinforcing components of a single institution. Building on this internal architecture, the paper develops the Realm of the Long Term and its Seven Pillars as the conditions for institutional endurance; a four-level framework of institutional success culminating in Legacy; a proposed conceptual vocabulary for twenty-first-century journalism; and a Triple Institutional Architecture spanning media, knowledge, and social-impact functions. The Model is situated within Nigeria's own tradition of the newspaper as intellectual institution, associated with Nnamdi Azikiwe and Obafemi Awolowo, and within a complementary global tradition linking journalism and disciplined inquiry, associated with Walter Lippmann and Hannah Arendt. It is grounded empirically in the newsroom's own production of three original analytical constructs—the Insecurity Triad, the Trinity of Sovereignty Decay, and the Decoupling Sovereignty Index—within a documented ninety-one-day period, offered here as an initial proof of concept rather than a generalisable finding. The paper situates the Model at the intersection of journalism and media studies, organisational theory, and strategic management, and closes with a discussion of its evidentiary limitations and a research agenda for testing, replicating, and adapting the framework across other newsrooms and institutional contexts, particularly within Africa and the wider Global South.

title: The Compounding Penalty of Cash Volatility: Reinvestment Interruption and Long-Horizon Equity Returns

detail.title: The Compounding Penalty of Cash Volatility: Reinvestment Interruption and Long-Horizon Equity Returns

detail.abstract: Two established bodies of research make opposite predictions about the same accounting quantity. Asset pricing theory treats variability in a firm's operating cash flow as a risk investors must be paid to bear, which implies higher expected returns for firms whose cash flows are erratic. The corporate finance and quality-investing literatures document the reverse, finding that unstable cash flows raise the cost of external capital, suppress investment, and reduce firm value. This paper reconciles the two by identifying a channel through which cash flow volatility lowers long-horizon shareholder wealth without operating as a discount rate effect. The mechanism is interrupted reinvestment. A firm whose operating cash flow falls short of its intended investment programme must either raise capital at a price that rises with its own instability or abandon the investment, and the resulting smaller capital base compounds for the remainder of the firm's life. The paper develops the measurement problem in detail, separates the proposed penalty from the arithmetic drag associated with volatile returns, and tests the channel on the operating cash flows of 3,080 United States firms drawn from mandatory filings between 2009 and 2026. The most stable quintile of firms outgrew the least stable by between 150 and 270 basis points a year over horizons of three to eight years, a difference significant at conventional levels, while the reinvestment behaviour the channel predicts did not appear: volatile firms invested more and borrowed less, not less and more. The data and procedures are drawn entirely from public sources.

title: Priced Beta, Unpriced Beta
affiliations: Bocconi University

detail.title: Priced Beta, Unpriced Beta

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing to declare
declarations.funderStatement: No funding

detail.abstract: The CAPM treats market beta as a sufficient statistic for priced aggregate risk. Yet expected returns compensate covariance with the stochastic discount factor, not covariance with the market itself. This distinction matters when some market fluctuations are orthogonal to the stochastic discount factor: they contribute to market volatility but not to the market risk premium. Market beta measures how much an asset covaries with the market, but not whether that covariance is generated by fluctuations relevant for marginal utility. I show that market beta combines exposure to priced and unpriced market variation. Under a priced-market spanning restriction, expected returns depend on priced beta, while unpriced beta has a zero structural price. Conventional beta therefore becomes an imperfect measure of compensated risk when assets load differently on the two components, generating CAPM pricing errors that increase with the difference in exposures. Empirically, priced and unpriced betas differ substantially across stocks. Consistent with the model, priced beta predicts average returns, unpriced beta carries little independent premium, and CAPM pricing errors increase with the exposure gap. Market beta's pricing performance therefore depends on what moves the market.

title: Closing the Gene Therapy Gap Early: Preparing a High-burden Health System for a Cure it cannot Yet afford

detail.title: Closing the Gene Therapy Gap Early: Preparing a High-burden Health System for a Cure it cannot Yet afford

detail.abstract:
Background. Two curative therapies for sickle cell disease were approved in the United States in December 2023 (US Food and Drug Administration, 2023), and England began treating eligible patients with one under a managed access arrangement in January 2025 (National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, 2025; NHS England, 2025). Approximately 79% of the world's affected births occur in sub-Saharan Africa (GBD 2021 Sickle Cell Disease Collaborators, 2023). The therapies exist where the disease largely does not, and remain absent where it is concentrated.

The pricing problem, quantified. Modelling of value-based prices across 13 countries produced base-case prices ranging from US$1,881 in Uganda to US$1.56 million in the United States, with scenario estimates ranging from US$676 to US$3.61 million. These differences reflect willingness-to-pay thresholds of US$120–3,228 per disability-adjusted life year averted in low- and middle-income countries versus US$33,016–100,000 in high-income countries (Morgan et al., 2024). A subsequent Ugandan analysis found one therapy potentially cost-effective at a scaled price when societal benefits are included (Montano-Campos et al., 2026).

Argument. This paper argues that price is the visible obstacle, not the binding one. Even at a price of a few thousand dollars, delivery would require capabilities Nigeria does not currently possess: a regulatory pathway for advanced therapy products; apheresis and transplant-grade centres; a patient registry capable of identifying and following candidates; and a health technology assessment function able to make and defend coverage decisions. Each requires years to build and cannot simply be procured when prices fall.

Contribution. The paper distinguishes preparatory capabilities that are justified regardless of whether
curative therapy ever arrives from those that are not, and recommends investment only in the former; specifies
what a credible refusal capability looks like and why it protects rather than restricts patients; and sets out the
equity claim that Nigerian institutions should be advancing now, while the pricing architecture for these
products is still being decided..

title: A Registry Worth Building: Designing a National Sickle Cell Register that Earns its Cost

detail.title: A Registry Worth Building: Designing a National Sickle Cell Register that Earns its Cost

detail.abstract:
Background. Nigeria's national guideline already requires a sickle cell disease registry integrated into the National Health Management Information System (Federal Ministry of Health, 2022). A registry also exists: the SickleInAfrica consortium enrolled 13,403 patients across Ghana, Nigeria and Tanzania between 2017 and 2021, including 6,572 patients in Nigeria across 22 facilities (Morrice et al., 2025). The policy question is therefore not whether Nigeria can build a registry, but what a national registry should be designed to achieve.

The central finding. SickleInAfrica provides a critical lesson for future registry design. The consortium defined 1,514 standardised data elements, but only 92 were collected across all facilities; after harmonisation, just 14 of those 92 were available and complete across every facility (Morrice et al., 2025). At one site, blood group data were up to 99.7% missing. A registry specified at 1,514 variables ultimately produced 14 consistently usable ones.

Argument. This paper argues that over-specification is a major failure mode of disease registries in low-resource health systems, driven by conflation of three distinct purposes: service delivery, research and accountability. These purposes require different datasets. A research-oriented registry may demand information that clinical staff cannot routinely provide, whereas a service-oriented registry is more likely to be completed because the data collected directly support patient care.

Contribution. The paper proposes a minimum viable national registry centred on service delivery rather than a research question: a defined dataset small enough to complete at every clinical contact; a rule that no field can be added without removing another; ownership within the routine health information system rather than a time-limited project; consent and governance aligned with the Nigeria Data Protection Act (Federal Republic of Nigeria, 2023); and a completeness-first quality standard informed by the English registry's coverage and consent performance (National Haemoglobinopathy Registry, 2023).

title: Taxonomy, Ontology, and Knowledge Graphs

detail.title: Taxonomy, Ontology, and Knowledge Graphs

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known personal, financial, or professional relationships with any individuals or organizations that could have influenced, or could be perceived to have influenced, the research presented in this study.

detail.abstract: The accelerating digitization of industrial and organizational environments has intensified the demand for principled methods of representing, organizing, and interrelating knowledge. Among the constructs most frequently invoked in this context are the taxonomy, the ontology, and the knowledge graph. Although these constructs are conceptually related and are often used interchangeably in professional discourse, they occupy distinct positions within the broader landscape of knowledge representation and serve functionally different purposes (Studer, Benjamins, & Fensel, 1998; Hogan et al., 2021). This paper presents a systematic conceptual and structural comparison of taxonomies, ontologies, and knowledge graphs, examining their formal definitions, characteristic properties, representational mechanisms, mutual relationships, and practical applications. A taxonomy is treated as a classificatory device that organizes concepts through hierarchical, predominantly is-a relationships. An ontology is treated, following Gruber (1993, 1995), as an explicit formal specification of a conceptualization, encompassing classes, properties, relationships, and axiomatic constraints. A knowledge graph is treated as a graph-structured, instance-level representation of entities and facts that is frequently, though not necessarily, governed by an ontology or comparable semantic schema (Fensel et al., 2020). Particular attention is directed toward the manufacturing domain, in which heterogeneous information originating from equipment, production processes, products, maintenance systems, enterprise applications, and industrial data infrastructures must be reconciled and integrated. The analysis is conducted at the conceptual level and is deliberately independent of any single software implementation, so that the resulting framework may be applied across differing technological environments. The paper argues that taxonomy, ontology, and knowledge graph should not be construed as competing or mutually substitutable technologies, but rather as complementary strata of a layered knowledgerepresentation architecture: the taxonomy furnishes classification, the ontology furnishes semantic structure, and the knowledge graph furnishes instantiated, interconnected knowledge. Establishing this distinction with precision is proposed as a necessary precondition for organizations seeking to design scalable semantic architectures and artificial-intelligence-enabled information systems.

title: Financing Liquidity with Capital or Information?

detail.title: Financing Liquidity with Capital or Information?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing to disclose.

detail.abstract: Standard decentralized market making requires liquidity providers to commit capital before demand arrives. We study what replaces this capital when market design becomes more capital efficient. Comparing constant-product and oracle-based market makers, we show that flatter pricing rules reduce capital requirements by weakening inventory-based price adjustment and increasing reliance on external price information. Using on-chain data from tokenized real-world assets, we find that capital efficiency is strongest near target inventories and deteriorates with inventory imbalances. Reference-price updates redirect order flow, while stale executable prices predict trader selection and adverse markouts, with stronger trading responses when inventory sensitivity is lower. Capital efficiency therefore substitutes information for balance-sheet capital in liquidity provision.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the environmental consequences of China's export slowdown during the mid-2010s. Using a shift-share design, we find that cities more exposed to the slowdown experienced significantly larger declines in PM 2.5 concentrations. However, only around 20% of this effect can be explained by the mechanical reduction in emissions caused by falling export production. The deeper mechanism operates through local officials' career incentives: adverse export shocks led higherlevel governments to assign stricter environmental targets to affected cities, raising the political salience of environmental performance. This, in turn, induced a clean-oriented industrial transformation within manufacturing, as selective policies and environmental regulations redirected resources away from polluting sectors and toward cleaner ones. As a result, low-export clean sectors expanded, experienced sizable productivity gains, and strengthened their comparative advantage, while polluting sectors contracted but shifted toward cleaner production. Further analysis suggests that the export shock ultimately pushed these regions toward a new development model-one increasingly driven by domestic demand and cleaner growth.
