detail.abstract: Can a city's investment-promotion policy retain its relative advantage as competing jurisdictions adopt policies targeting the same industry? We study this question in China using an auditable LLM-assisted protocol that classifies 943 of 4,124 documents as core policies and links the resulting 2000-2024 city-industry policy events to firm registrations across 335 cities and 19 industries. Using only 1995-1999 information, we construct fixed, directed, industryspecific competitor networks. Horizon-specific samples retain recurrent policy-window observations and restrict the comparison state to observations from city-industry cells with no observed policy event or to pre-first-event observations from cells with a later observed event. We estimate unweighted OLS triple-interaction models with city-industry, city-year, and industryyear fixed effects. The models estimate how the effect of the focal policy on a city's nationwide same-industry entry share varies with one-year-lagged weighted peer-policy coverage and baseline income. In the main specification, a 10-percentage-point increase in peer coverage reduces the estimated effect of the focal policy by 0.027 percentage points at the 90th percentile of 1999 income, produces almost no change at mean income, and increases the estimated policy effect by 0.023 percentage points at the 10th percentile. This pattern holds across alternative policy windows, competitor networks, and entry outcomes: greater peerpolicy coverage weakens the estimated policy effect in higher-income cities and strengthens it in lower-income cities.

title: Copula-based Measures of Extreme Dependence
affiliations: McGill University, Department of Economics., Peking University - Guanghua School of Management and University of Liverpool Management School

detail.title: Copula-based Measures of Extreme Dependence

detail.abstract: We propose new measures of extreme dependence based on Kullback-Leibler relative entropy and defined in terms of the copula density. By reformulating tail exceedance functionals through the copula, we relocate the problem to the unit square and avoid the boundary and tail-instability issues inherent in kernel density methods traditionally used in the entropy literature. For estimation, we employ the Bernstein copula density estimator and show that, under standard mixing and smoothing conditions, its approximation bias is asymptotically negligible, allowing us to obtain consistent nonparametric estimators together with their Bahadur-type representations. These results lead to an asymptotically pivotal test for symmetric tail dependence whose limiting distribution is free of tuning parameters. We analyze the properties of the test under both global and local alternatives and establish the validity of a bootstrap version suitable for finite samples. A Monte Carlo simulation study shows that the bootstrap-based tests exhibit good finite-sample size and power properties across various data-generating processes and sample sizes. Finally, we present an empirical application that highlights the practical utility of the extreme dependence measures. Specifically, we quantify the degree of extreme dependence between the US financial market and several developed and emerging financial markets.

detail.abstract: In this paper, we discover and formalize the Prober Scaling Laws for semantic cloze forensics, building upon the foundations of Paper 1 [1] and Paper 2 [2]. Scaling cloze probers from 12B to 120B parameters increases propositional meaning recovery ($M$) from $52.54\%$ to $60.64\%$ and widens the net separation margin to $+50.24\%$. Furthermore, Zhipu AI GLM's native bidirectional blank-infilling architecture achieves a state-of-the-art $60.77\%$ propositional recovery and $+51.16\%$ meaning gap with an effect size of $\text{Cohen's } d = 5.62$ ($p < 10^{-14}$). ClozeCongruence establishes new SOTA records on RAID ($99.58\%$ AUROC, $+11.38\%$ gain), HC3 ($99.98\%$ AUROC), MGTBench ($99.58\%$ Acc), and Ghostbuster ($99.62\%$ F1), while delivering $100.00\%$ top-1 attribution accuracy across 30 deep academic essays.

detail.abstract: U.S. equity returns are known to be higher overnight, on Fridays, in January, around the turn of the month, and during macroeconomic announcement windows. We replicate 153 long-short factors and document the mirror image of these patterns: factor premia are systematically lower in exactly the same periods. On average, a factor loses 2.01 bps overnight but earns 5.45 bps intraday; it earns 5.77 bps on Mondays versus 1.24 bps on Fridays; and its returns are significantly lower in January, at the turn of the month, and around macroeconomic announcements. The reversed calendar effects persist out of sample and strengthen when news sentiment is elevated, consistent with sentiment-driven mispricing.

title: The Feasibility Era is over: Thirty Years of Retail Age Assurance and the Reallocation of Duty in Platform Child Safety

detail.title: The Feasibility Era is over: Thirty Years of Retail Age Assurance and the Reallocation of Duty in Platform Child Safety

detail.abstract: For two decades, platforms facing demands to identify and protect minor users have answered with one defense in several costumes: it cannot be done. Age assurance online is said to be infeasible, an undue burden, or a fundamental alteration of the service. This Article closes that defense with two records the debate has never joined. The first is historical: American retail has run the age-assurance experiment at national scale since the early 1990s. The voluntary arm, the Entertainment Software Rating Board, drove underage purchase rates for Mature-rated games from 85 percent in 2000 to 13 percent by 2011 with no legal compulsion; the mandatory arm, the Synar program for tobacco, spent federal money and sixteen years reaching the same number. The arms converged, and the residual failure mode in both was never the gate; it was the credentialed adult who walked through it. The second record is the industry's own: the executed August 2026 Meta settlement, which sets audited false-positive ceilings of 3 percent for users thirteen to fifteen and 10 percent for sixteen to seventeen and obligates an under-13 detection model against auditor-supervised enforcement targets, and the production deployment of machine-learning age estimation that infers minority regardless of the birthday supplied. A defendant cannot contract to perform what it litigates as impossible. The Article then cashes the feasibility fact where it decides elements. In the pending products litigation, the court has held that age verification is a product actionable past Section 230 while leaving the feasibility of alternative designs unlitigated; the admissions are that missing proof, a reasonable alternative design not hypothesized but contracted, priced, and shipped. In accommodation law, undue burden and fundamental alteration are defenses the entity must demonstrate, and an entity that has warranted the capability elsewhere cannot demonstrate its impossibility. And in First Amendment tailoring after Free Speech Coalition, Inc. v. Paxton, feasibility evidence hinges the scrutiny analysis, and the retail record is the evidentiary base beneath the Court's description of age verification as traditional and legitimate. With feasibility closed, what remains is duty allocation, a design-defaults question the platform owns.

title: Real-Time Recovery of Structural Shocks from High-Frequency Data

detail.title: Real-Time Recovery of Structural Shocks from High-Frequency Data

detail.abstract: How should a macroeconomic model whose grid is quarterly read data that arrive daily? Aggregating the fast series to the slow grid destroys the information a realtime observer needs most-the within-window movements that are the structural shocks themselves-and refining the grid cannot restore it under the standard representation of flows. This paper develops a continuous-time, mixed-frequency filtering framework that reads each release on its own calendar and delivers both objects of real-time interest online: the latent state and the contemporaneous structural shocks hitting the economy. Identification rests on a measurement primitive: a reported flow is the window increment of a cumulative observable and inherits the state's Brownian increment-the pass-through-read instantaneously by a correlated-noise Kalman-Bucy filter. Four closed-form factors and a recovery-correlation law separate what finer sampling repairs from what only the correct representation can; Monte Carlo evidence in two New Keynesian economies verifies each factor. Daily observation of a single financial stock cuts the tracking error of a never-directly-observed state nearly thirtyfold and rescues the weakly identified shock, while densification under the wrong primitive makes filtering worse, not better. The proposed misspecification tests maintain the transparency of the underlying structural constraints

detail.abstract: Reliable routing is critical for large-scale banking ATM networks operating over 4G/5G cellular connectivity. This paper presents a real-world case study of approximately 3,000 ATM sites and examines operational limitations observed in a legacy tunnel-based architecture using per-site BGP sessions. In the legacy design, loss of mobile connectivity could leave tunnel and routing states temporarily inconsistent with actual site reachability, resulting in stale routes, traffic blackholing, delayed failure detection, and increased operational overhead. The deployment was migrated to a Route Behind Mobile Station (RBMS) architecture using RADIUS-based route provisioning, where route installation and withdrawal are associated with the mobile session lifecycle. Operational observations reported for the deployment indicate reductions in routing overhead, convergence time, core-router CPU utilization, and troubleshooting effort. The study does not introduce a new RADIUS routing mechanism; rather, it documents and evaluates the operational use of session-aware route management compared with per-site tunnel/BGP routing in a large cellular ATM environment.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the valuation, token economics, market structure, and risk profile of HYPE, the native token of Hyperliquid, an on-chain derivatives and financial infrastructure platform. The analysis focuses on the economic relationship between Hyperliquid's protocol activity and HYPE through the Assistance Fund's open-market acquisition and permanent burn mechanism, while separating token utility from legal equity ownership. It evaluates HYPE using multiple annualized protocol-revenue methodologies, revenue-multiple frameworks, supply and dilution analysis, and a scenario-based valuation framework. The paper also examines the August 2026 repricing through regulatory catalysts, derivatives positioning, liquidity, and market structure, and assesses Hyperliquid's competitive position, regulatory exposure, ecosystem expansion, and reflexivity risks. The analysis finds that HYPE possesses an unusually direct and measurable value-capture mechanism, but that the token's valuation already embeds substantial expectations for revenue durability, market-share retention, ecosystem diversification, and continued supply absorption. The paper concludes with explicit conditions under which the investment thesis would strengthen or fail.

detail.abstract: Common-interest developments house tens of millions of Americans and increasingly assign homeowners' associations functions once performed by municipalities. This Article examines physically gated communities as a particularly visible subset of that broader system. It argues that mandatory private residential governance can provide valued services while also creating problems of accountability, amendment, public access, and regional coordination. The Article combines doctrinal analysis, institutional theory, and descriptive housing data; because no national dataset precisely enumerates gated communities, its population estimates are presented as approximations rather than census counts. The Article also presents a stylized voting model showing how amendment provisions measured against all eligible owners can create institutional lock-in when participation is low. The model is illustrative rather than predictive: its central result follows from the interaction among the denominator, the approval threshold, turnout, and support among participating owners. The Article then evaluates state and local reforms, including judicial threshold-reduction procedures, quorum-sensitive voting rules, transparency protections, and prospective infrastructure conditions. Its contribution is to connect property theory, commons governance, local-government law, and democratic accountability without treating either privatization or municipal control as categorically superior.

detail.abstract: Can governments improve governance durably without expanding enforcement capacity? This paper shows that time-limited campaign-style enforcement can generate persistent gains by activating citizen participation. Using China's Central Environmental Inspection with a dynamic panel estimator and a difference-indifferences strategy, I find the campaign improves air quality by 4–9% in the long run, concentrated in SO2 and PM2.5, and increase complaints by about 40%. Effects are amplified where NGO capacity is stronger. A theoretical framework explains persistence through citizens' belief updating about government responsiveness. The findings suggest campaigns offer a cost-effective path to durable governance improvements in capacity-constrained settings.

detail.abstract: This paper presents an outcome-based enforcement audit of France's response to gender-based violence (GBV), using consolidated 2024 administrative data published by the Ministry of the Interior's statistical service (SSMSI) and the Ministry of Justice's statistical service (SSER). Rather than evaluating statutory design or policy intent, the analysis isolates the enforcement chain (reporting, prosecutorial filtering, judicial conversion, sentencing, and protection-order compliance) to test whether legal protections translate into enforceable outcomes. Applying the Lex Feminae Index outcome-based audit methodology, the paper finds that France maintains a comprehensive statutory framework and an active, well-documented investigative and judicial apparatus, yet judicial conversion from identified suspect to final conviction remains structurally narrow: approximately 29% for intimate partner violence and 8.9% for rape in the 2024 cycle. Attrition concentrates disproportionately at the prosecutorial-activation stage rather than at trial, a pattern consistent with the comparative "justice gap" literature on sexual-violence attrition. The absence of a codified femicide offense and of a unified breach-to-sanction dataset for judicial protection orders further constrain offence-level traceability. These findings place France's 2024 enforcement performance below the threshold the Index reserves for demonstrated protection delivery, notwithstanding an operational legal and institutional architecture, and are situated within the broader European enforcement-gap literature and the Council of Europe's Istanbul Convention monitoring findings on France.

title: When Care Becomes Control: Cumulative and Gendered Harmful Parenting in Contemporary Indian Families
affiliations: Manipal University Jaipur, Manipal University Jaipur, Amity University Kolkata and Manipal University Jaipur

detail.title: When Care Becomes Control: Cumulative and Gendered Harmful Parenting in Contemporary Indian Families
detail.abstract: Background: While evidence indicates a high rate of child maltreatment in India, there remains a dearth of studies that examine harmful parenting as a patterned social issue. Objective: The study examined how harmful parenting experiences co-occur in contemporary Indian families and how gender shapes exposure to these experiences. Participants and Setting: We collected data from 446 young adults aged 18–25 years who completed a culturally grounded 20-item survey. Methods: Because the step-parent item was conditional, our analysis used a retained 19-item harmful parenting measure. Internal consistency, Mokken scale analysis, latent class analysis, chi-square tests, multinomial logistic regression, and corrected gender comparisons were used. Results: The retained measure showed strong internal consistency and moderate cumulative scalability. Latent class analysis identified low-, moderate-, and high-exposure classes. Female respondents were disproportionately represented in the high-exposure class, and item-level comparisons showed higher reported exposure among female respondents for role enforcement, privacy invasion, harsh words, lifestyle control, body shaming, and conditional support, all of which remained significant after Holm–Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusions: These findings suggest that harmful parenting in everyday Indian family life is better understood as a cumulative, gendered structure of control and emotional harm.

title: AI's Next Failure: Governance, Not Models
affiliations: The Digital Economist and The Digital Economist

detail.title: AI's Next Failure: Governance, Not Models

detail.abstract:
Governing Artificial Intelligence in Education argues that the effectiveness of AI governance in education is shaped less by the strength of regulatory design and more by the capacity to implement, operationalize, and sustain policy within real institutional environments. The brief examines how the United States and the European Union approach AI governance through contrasting models—one decentralized and implementation-driven, the other structured and risk-based—and shows how both systems encounter similar limitations when policies are not translated into practice. Drawing on comparative analysis, it highlights how gaps in institutional capacity, data governance, and oversight mechanisms contribute to uneven outcomes, persistent inequities, and limited evidence of impact on learning and decision-making.
‍
This policy brief proposes a shift from principle-based governance toward implementation-focused frameworks that prioritize operational clarity, institutional readiness, and continuous evaluation. It outlines key policy priorities, including strengthening human and technical capacity, embedding accountability into decision-making processes, and establishing mechanisms to assess how AI systems affect educational outcomes over time. Intended for policymakers, education leaders, and institutional stakeholders, the brief positions AI governance not as a purely regulatory challenge but as a systems-level coordination problem, where effective outcomes depend on aligning policy design with the realities of educational practice.

detail.abstract: This study examines the personal finance habits of college students, focusing on their saving behavior, spending patterns, income sources, and awareness of investment options such as mutual funds and stocks. Data was collected through a structured survey distributed via Google Forms and WhatsApp, targeting undergraduate and postgraduate students across multiple academic years, yielding 103 responses within 22 hours. The findings reveal that while 66% of respondents are aware of basic financial concepts, only 30% have actually invested, indicating a significant gap between financial awareness and financial action. The majority of students (93%) remain dependent on parental income, with food accounting for the largest share of monthly expenditure. Notably, students report learning about personal finance primarily through informal channels such as YouTube, Instagram, and peer networks rather than formal education, suggesting a gap in structured financial literacy programs. The study also identifies a modest gender gap in financial awareness, with male respondents showing higher awareness (69%) than female respondents (61%). These findings highlight the need for accessible, structured financial literacy initiatives targeted at college students to bridge the gap between financial knowledge and real-world financial behavior.

title: The Execution-Certainty Wedge: Why Contention-Linked Instruments Redistribute at Near-Zero Cost, and Per-Entity Caps Do Not
affiliations: Universidad de Buenos Aires

detail.title: The Execution-Certainty Wedge: Why Contention-Linked Instruments Redistribute at Near-Zero Cost, and Per-Entity Caps Do Not

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no personal or financial relationship with any person or organisation that could be perceived to have influenced this work. The research was carried out independently, was not commissioned, and no party reviewed or approved it prior to submission.

detail.abstract:
In several important markets the party doing the allocating does not rank offers by value. It ranks them by effective value — what is offered, multiplied by the probability the transaction actually completes. Where one class of participant holds a systematic advantage in that second factor, the winner is not reliably the highest-value participant, and the disadvantage falls on those who cannot supply certainty: the buyer who needs a mortgage, the applicant who must compare financial-aid offers before committing, the patient whose insurer loses one claim in six. This paper names that gap the execution-certainty wedge, documents it in three markets, and establishes what follows for policy.
The measured case is residential real estate. Reher and Valkanov (2024) estimate a mortgage-cash premium of 11.7% across 426,256 repeat-sales transactions, 8.6% in offer-level brokerage data and 10.5% in a homeowner survey, against a rationally justified compensation for transaction failure of 3.3% for a representative seller, or 6.9% adjusting for heterogeneity in local denial rates. The premium exceeds its actuarial justification by roughly four to eight percentage points, and that excess, not the whole premium, is the distortion available for correction.
An agent-based model of a shared-inventory market compares four allocation regimes against a policy-invariant benchmark, and the central result is a ranking of instruments. At the calibrated wedge, a smooth duty triggered by a local contention signal cuts owner-occupier starvation from 41.9% to 36.6% at an aggregate welfare cost of zero; a work-conserving fair share cuts it to 24.7% for 1.8% of aggregate welfare; a static per-entity acquisition cap — the instrument most often proposed — cuts it to 8.7% but costs 11.3% of aggregate welfare, 17.3% once supply responds, and decays to a statistical no-op once the same capital is held across twenty-five shell entities. Constraints that bind on observed contention survive every robustness test applied; constraints that bind on entity identity survive none.
Two results are methodological and transfer beyond this setting. Measuring allocative efficiency in a market where the policy determines who is waiting requires a benchmark fixed independently of the policy; a contemporaneous benchmark computed over the bidders each regime leaves in the queue moves by up to 14% across regimes and reverses the sign of the conclusion. And a latency statistic computed over completed transactions is uninterpretable without the accompanying rate at which participants leave unserved — a rule that applies identically to housing search times and to clinical waiting lists.
Four boundary conditions state when the underlying scheduling correspondence transfers to institutions — assignable identity, flow rather than stock, an insulated scheduler, and unified rather than partitioned enforcement — and each is matched to a regime in force whose operating record displays the predicted behaviour. Because identity is assignable in admissions and in health but manufacturable in property markets, the conditions generate a testable prediction: the per-entity cap that fails in housing should succeed in the other two.

title: Pollution Pricing in Equilibrium: Production, Reallocation, and Aggregate Impacts
affiliations: Indiana University, University of Texas at Austin and Cornell University - Charles H. Dyson School of Applied Economics and Management

detail.title: Pollution Pricing in Equilibrium: Production, Reallocation, and Aggregate Impacts
detail.abstract:
How much does pricing pollution cut aggregate emissions, and at what cost? We develop a microfounded equilibrium model of firm production and abatement that can be estimated from standard firm financial and emissions data, without observing abatement effort directly. The model captures three adjustment margins: short-run input substitution, reallocation of output from dirty to cleaner firms, and long-run clean technology adoption. Applying it to the first 17 years of the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU-ETS), we find input substitution is rigid: firms cannot cut emissions in the short run without cutting output. Reallocation instead drives nearly all of the short-run aggregate emissions response, concentrated in sectors with heterogeneous emissions intensities, like power and cement, or with elastic demand, like refining. Clean technology adoption also responds causally to permit price shocks, reducing firms’ emissions intensity over the five years that follow. Doubling the permit price cuts aggregate emissions 23% in the short run and 31% in the longer run after induced clean technology adoption. In the short run, output falls by 4%, primarily because carbon costs pass from upstream polluting industries like electricity to downstream producers. In the long run, output falls just 2.5%, as clean technology adoption dampens these supply-chain impacts. Carbon pricing thus delivers substantial emissions reductions with moderate output effects, and much of the economic burden falls on downstream firms through higher upstream input costs.

title: Spillover Effects of Transfer Programs
affiliations: University of Rochester, Université Clermont Auvergne and University of Utah

detail.title: Spillover Effects of Transfer Programs
detail.abstract:
We derive four facts from experiments on the spillover effects of cash and in-kind transfer programs onto non-recipients: (1) average spillovers on consumption and asset value are negligible; (2) negative psychological spillovers emerge in the longer term among households randomly excluded from transfers by within-village lotteries; (3) these spillovers are concentrated in consumption-poor households; and (4) they do not appear when the selection of transfer recipients is eligibility-based. These findings are consistent with household preferences against within-village randomization of transfers, and point to additional benefits of cluster-level randomized designs over household-level ones.

title: Can Private Markets Fill the Gap? Graduate Student Lending After the Elimination of GradPLUS
affiliations: University of Virginia

detail.title: Can Private Markets Fill the Gap? Graduate Student Lending After the Elimination of GradPLUS
detail.abstract:
The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA, P.L. 119-21) eliminates the federal GradPLUS loan program for new borrowers effective July 1, 2026, replacing nearly two decades of uncapped federal graduate lending with annual limits of $20,500 ($50,000 for eleven professional fields) and new aggregate caps. The resulting financing gap — approximately $8 billion annually across roughly 370,000 affected borrowers — raises the question of whether and how private capital will substitute for displaced federal lending.This paper analyzes the economics of that transition. Before GradPLUS, private lenders filled the gap between federal Stafford limits and graduate program costs, with nonfederal graduate originations reaching $5.3 billion (constant 2024 dollars) by 2005–06. After GradPLUS extended federal borrowing to the full cost of attendance in 2006, private lending collapsed — falling more than 70 percent within a few years and never recovering. The federal program provided not only credit but, through income-driven repayment and Public Service Loan Forgiveness, insurance against earnings risk that no private product could replicate. The same features that crowded out private lending generated compounding distortions: borrowing untethered to repayment capacity, upward pressure on tuition, and a reversal from projected federal surpluses to losses exceeding thirty cents per GradPLUS dollar lent.Linking institution-by-field federal borrowing data to institution-by-field earnings outcomes, I examine the relationship between historical borrowing above the new OBBBA caps and post-completion earnings across programs. I find substantial variation in the extent to which different degree programs would likely support above-cap borrowing from private lenders or other sources. In fields such as law and MBA, earnings rise steeply with borrowing exposure, providing a basis for program-level risk pricing; in fields such as social work, counseling psychology, and physical therapy, the earnings-to-borrowing gradient is essentially flat. I also examine features of the private capital market and institutional responses shaping the transition — including capital constraints on scaling private lending, legal barriers to using program-level outcomes data in underwriting, and the emerging role of institutions as intermediaries between lenders and students.

detail.abstract: Who can challenge a tax assessment is a question of capacity and standing. When a natural or legal person dies, is dissolved, is amalgamated, or becomes bankrupt, it can be difficult to know who (if anyone) can be assessed tax and who has standing to dispute the assessment. While recent Supreme Court of Canada decisions clarify in which court a tax dispute may be decided, they do not address who can participate in those disputes. The case law on who can appeal an assessment to the Tax Court of Canada has developed unevenly. The leading tax case on dissolved corporations, 145 Ontario, overturned the prior appellate decision, 495187 Ontario, for being manifestly wrong. However, cases addressing the question have rarely analyzed capacity and standing at the Tax Court through the lens of the appeal rights in the tax statutes and have instead relied on private-law concepts as a complete answer. Although private law has an important role in the analysis, the statutory regime for tax disputes must also be considered. The Tax Court of Canada Act grants the Tax Court jurisdiction to hear appeals arising from certain statutes, including the Income Tax Act (ITA). Section 169 of the ITA permits a taxpayer to appeal an assessment to the Tax Court. In some examples, legal fictions in the ITA extend appeal rights to non-entities under private law. Further, the private law itself contains legal fictions that extend rights to non-entities, including dissolved corporations. The time is ripe to revisit the capacity and standing of a “taxpayer” under assessment, objection, and appeal provisions of the tax law. The current landscape allows tax authorities to assess taxpayers in situations where they have no appeal rights, which contravenes a recognized principle of procedural fairness. Taxpayers would benefit from clarity on the rights of an entity to object and appeal after death, amalgamation, dissolution, or bankruptcy and, where those rights exist, the process for giving authority to a person to act on behalf of the entity.

detail.abstract: Canada’s tax administration is undergoing rapid digital transformation under tight fiscal constraints, yet reforms are still assessed mainly by their cost and revenue impact. This article introduces the marginal value of public funds for tax administration (MVPFTaxAdmin), a welfare-based framework for measuring the social return per administrative dollar spent. The framework integrates efficiency, equity, and public value into a unified assessment of how administrative design affects taxpayers’ welfare and trust. Using a stylized case study of automatic tax filing, the article shows how the MVPFTaxAdmin ratio increases once accessibility and legitimacy are incorporated alongside efficiency. Automatic filing can yield high social returns by improving access for lowcapacity taxfilers. The MVPF-TaxAdmin framework provides policy makers with a practical tool to prioritize administration modernization based on inclusive welfare metrics.

title: Canaries in the Gold Mine: Early Productivity Gains from Artificial Intelligence Creating Organization Capital
affiliations: , Robert H. Smith School of Business and Robert H. Smith School of Business

detail.title: Canaries in the Gold Mine: Early Productivity Gains from Artificial Intelligence Creating Organization Capital
detail.abstract:
Using a new firm-level measure of AI investment based on AI-skilled employment—spanning machine learning through generative and agentic AI—we show that AI investments are associated with productivity growth in recent years, but not over the previous decade. We trace the productivity gains to the accumulation of organization capital that AI helps create: durable firm-specific knowledge acquired through learning-by-doing that enables more efficient production. We build a novel measure of organization capital based on workers’ job descriptions and document that productivity gains are driven by AI-skilled jobs that build organization capital. Overall, our findings suggest that AI investment generates productivity growth by creating organization capital.

title: A Deep Case for Shallow Integration
affiliations: Princeton University and Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Department of Economics, University of California, San Diego (UCSD) - Department of Economics

detail.title: A Deep Case for Shallow Integration
detail.abstract:
We study international cooperation in a general environment with pecuniary and non-pecuniary externalities across countries. We derive two main theorems, each demonstrating that market-access commitments, a form of shallow integration, are sufficient to implement globally efficient policies. When all cross-border externalities are pecuniary, the first theorem provides a new and unifying perspective on a series of results by Bagwell and Staiger. When some cross-border externalities are non-pecuniary, the second theorem shows that market-access commitments, properly extended, still sustain global efficiency. These extended market-access commitments reinterpret cross-border externalities as additional goods that are traded and priced at their social values. We discuss the implications for international cooperation on climate change and geopolitics.

detail.abstract:
Organizational field theory operates on a productive ambiguity: it grants cognition and agency to institutions, regimes, and fields, and treats the actors whose interactions those aggregates presumably summarize as passive terminals. This move is explanatorily convenient and ontologically
expensive. I propose the SRI framework – Symbolic systems, Resources, Interests – to restore the missing rigor without sacrificing the field-theoretic tradition’s empirical purchase. The framework rests on nine epistemological constraints (R), twelve constructs (C) that operationalize the actor as
a non-reductive atom, one axiom of wide interaction (A1), and six propositions (E2-E7) linking constructs to testable claims. Two contributions deserve emphasis. First, the bi-locational reading of probabilistic calculability reframes a long-standing quarrel between rational-choice and behavioral traditions by making the analyst’s position explicit. Second, the multimodal cavity of the field names the operative site of situated action, ontologically triangulated with the concrete action system and the field along the axis of time (intra-, inter-, trans-temporal). The framework is atomistic in a technical sense – non-reductive methodological individualism, not Hobbesian atomism – and embodied and enactive after Merleau-Ponty, Damasio, Maturana and Varela, Noë, and Suchman. It offers a lens, not a theory of everything, and declares its scope conditions openly.
Empirical demonstration is reserved for the companion papers of the series. The framework provides a rigorous basis for analyzing organizational  failure and institutional change in high-velocity environments.

detail.abstract: When a maritime chokepoint is already impaired, a key question for freight-derivative pricing is how long that impairment will persist. The pricing implications are contract-specific because routes differ in physical exposure and delivery periods differ in settlement-window exposure under the same restoration outlook. To quantify this settlement exposure, we develop a settlement-average framework that maps prediction-market restoration-deadline prices into a contract-aligned impairment share for each Forward Freight Agreement (FFA) settlement window. In the 2026 Strait of Hormuz disruption, we align changes in this measure with exact-contract returns on Baltic dirty-tanker FFAs over the same assessment intervals. A 10-percentage-point upward update in the impairment share is associated with about 3.5 log points of repricing on the directly exposed Middle East Gulf to China route relative to the non-Hormuz benchmark basket. The relation is concentrated on the exposed leg, while the entirely non-Hormuz spread loads near zero. The pooled estimate is identified mainly by across-date shifts in the traded restoration curve. Against like-for-like historical exact-contract windows, the event-window studentized statistic exceeds all 90 full-support comparators and remains in the right tail under broader reference sets. A conditional calibration implies an impaired-state freight-rate uplift of about 44 percent on the exposed route. More broadly, the approach provides charterers, shipowners, and freight-risk managers with a forward-looking measure of contract-level maritime disruption exposure as the traded restoration outlook evolves before physical recovery is observed.

detail.abstract: Crewed Earth-Mars transportation is a coupled propulsion, trajectory, vehicle-sizing, and mission-duration problem. This paper derives an exact break-even condition between chemical propulsion, nuclear thermal propulsion (NTP), and hybrid allocation under an explicit linear NTP-specific mass penalty, and reconciles that model against an executed ephemeris-based trajectory calculation rather than an assumed ΔV. Two cases are reported. The illustrative case (ΔV = 4.833 km/s, terminal mass 100 t, chemical Isp = 455 s, NTP Isp = 900 s) gives an ideal initial mass of 295.394 t for allchemical propulsion and 172.908 t for all-NTP propulsion-a 41.47% reduction-with break-even penalty thresholds of 92.601 t and 158.199 t. The reconciled case uses an ephemeris-based Lambert trajectory computed for the 27 June 2035 / 200-day transfer window (patched-conic total ΔV ≈ 5.748 km/s) in place of the assumed figure, giving 362.627 t / 191.795 t (47.11% reduction) and revised thresholds of 122.163 t and 230.973 t. All headline claims in this paper use the reconciled case; the illustrative case is retained only to show the model's sensitivity to its ΔV input. The paper distinguishes three evidence classes throughout: closed-form analytical results (executed and verified), a scoped external benchmark comparison against NASA DRA 5.0 and Copernicus literature that now sources or margin-brackets five of six non-payload hardware terms (engine, reactor, shield, truss, tankage, power/thermal), and an explicitly out-of-scope high-fidelity optimization layer, which is described but not claimed as executed.

detail.abstract: The rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) creates new opportunities for strategic content generation on online platforms, including potentially harmful forms of manipulation that may undermine platform effectiveness and reshape platform dynamics. However, measuring such activity is difficult because AI-generated content is rarely directly observable. We introduce an empirical approach that leverages discrete LLM supply shocks-abrupt changes in model prices and capabilities, and contrasts verified with non-verified reviews to identify changes in platform activity associated with generative AI supply improvements. We apply this approach to more than 13 million reviews from Trustpilot, one of the leading online platforms for business reviews. A robust finding is that following LLM supply shocks, unverified reviews shift toward greater negativity: more 1-stars, fewer 5-stars, and lower ratings, with effects driven primarily by new model releases and concentrated among firms with the lowest and highest review volumes, suggesting that strategic AI use may reshape platform competition dynamics. We further find that LLM supply shocks trigger short, concentrated bursts of review activity. Together, these findings suggest that generative AI is already reshaping how reputation and competition operate on online platforms.

title: Calendar Congestion and Trading Responses: Cornerstone Lock-up Expirations in Hong Kong IPOs

detail.abstract: Contractual lock-ups make previously restricted shares eligible to trade on dates fixed months in advance. This paper asks whether the trading response to a Hong Kong IPO cornerstone release depends on other releases reaching the market on the same session. Congestion is formed from a frozen pre-outcome census of 504 eligible release events; the focal sample contains 226 complete event windows for 2022-2025 listing cohorts. The primary equal-event specification models log(1 + event-session volume relative to the preceding-20-session mean), retains 11 zero-volume sessions, and controls for market turnover, issuer size, and pre-event liquidity. The crowded-session coefficient is 0.432 (event-session clustered p = 0.010) and its interaction with log(1 + release strength) is-0.683 (p = 0.018). Event-week clustering, wildcluster bootstrap inference, month-constrained calendar randomization, alternative same-session congestion measures, placebo dates, and joint omission of the most crowded sessions support the negative interaction. The result is scale-sensitive: asinh and positive-only log outcomes agree, but an untransformed volume-ratio model and a Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood share-flow model do not. Holm adjustment across volume, return, and volatility interactions gives p = 0.054; neither price nor range volatility is robust. The evidence therefore describes a typical-event transformed-volume pattern, strongest among smaller releases. It does not establish aggregate share-flow pressure, price dislocation, or a causal market-capacity mechanism.

title: Paris Five-star Hotel Quality Benchmark 2026: Executive Summary, May 2023–May 2026

detail.title: Paris Five-star Hotel Quality Benchmark 2026: Executive Summary, May 2023–May 2026

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the Founder & CEO of HotScore Analytics, which developed the proprietary HotScore™ methodology used in this study. No external organization funded or influenced the analysis, and no hotel paid for inclusion or preferential treatment in the benchmark.
declarations.funderStatement: The research was internally funded by HotScore Analytics. No external funding was received.

detail.abstract:
This report presents a three-year benchmark of guest-perceived quality across the five-star hotel market in Paris between May 2023 and May 2026. The analysis is based on 121,959 validated guest reviews and uses the proprietary HotScore™ methodology to examine market-wide quality performance, competitive structure and changes over time.

The study compares three consecutive annual evaluation periods, including the exceptional demand environment surrounding the Paris 2024 Olympic Games and the subsequent post-Olympic period. It examines changes in the average market HotScore, the proportion of hotels performing above the annual destination benchmark, the stability of the Top 10, and differences between global branded, regional branded and independent hotels.

The findings indicate that guest-perceived quality reached its highest level during the Olympic-period evaluation and subsequently moderated, while remaining above the pre-Olympic baseline. The analysis also identifies unusually stable leadership at the top of the market: Four Seasons Hotel George V ranked first in all three annual evaluations, while only four hotels remained in the Top 10 throughout the full period.

At market level, global branded and independent hotels recorded broadly similar average HotScores. However, global branded hotels accounted for 70% of all Top 10 positions, while global branded hotels together with independent properties affiliated with Small Luxury Hotels of the World or The Leading Hotels of the World accounted for 93.3% of Top 10 positions across the three-year period.

The report further examines hotel scale and finds no evidence that larger luxury hotels face an inherent guest-experience disadvantage. Overall, the analysis illustrates how large-scale guest feedback can provide an additional benchmark for understanding hotel quality, competitive positioning and destination-level hospitality performance.

title: Who Audits the Watchdogs? A Reproducibility Audit of the 853-Paper IHU-Mi Ethics Investigation

detail.abstract: Frank et al. reported ethical or legal concerns in 853 publications associated with the Institut Hospitalo-Universitaire Méditerranée Infection (IHU-Mi), including a headline finding that 304 of 374 publications with recovered approval documents were inconsistent with those approvals. Because the article functions simultaneously as scholarship, a record of authors’ complaints to journals, and support for continuing correction of a large publication corpus, its own evidentiary chain warrants unusually close scrutiny. This public-record audit compares the version of record, its frozen 853-row supplementary CSV, Table 1, Figure 2, the open peer-review record, official PubMed documentation, and a PLOS editorial resolution retained in the cohort. The audit identifies central numerical contradictions: 304 versus 283 approval mismatches and 235 versus 229 articles said to fall outside approval 09-022. The frozen CSV reproduces 75 retrospective-approval labels and 426 healthy-participant labels, but only 190 explicit overseas-without-local-approval labels rather than 194, and 330 blank approval fields rather than the reported 343. It contains no case-level variables for the 304/374 or 283/374 mismatch determinations, no inclusion/exclusion decision variable, no assessor identities, no coding or consensus record, and no frozen editorial-outcome snapshot. Table 1 contains 430 approval-publication instances, Figure 2 contains 442 across one fewer approval row, and the CSV does not supply a multi-approval mapping capable of reconciling either total with 374 unique publications. Duplicate DOI and preprint/publication records, unsupported retrospective labels, impossible negative review intervals, a retained case whose ethics concern PLOS had already declared resolved, and unresolved peer-review requests for a replicable protocol further weaken auditability. These findings do not rebut independently documented failures at IHU-Mi. They establish that criticism of those failures cannot exempt the critics’ own high-impact claims from reproducibility standards. The proportionate response is immediate correction of indisputable errors, preservation and independent reconstruction of the analysis, and an Expression of Concern if reconciliation cannot be completed promptly. Retraction becomes appropriate only if the central findings cannot be reconstructed or remain materially unreliable after audit.

title: The Anatomy and Evolution of Survey Error
affiliations: University of Chicago, , University of Virginia,  and Government of the United States of America - Internal Revenue Service (IRS)

detail.title: The Anatomy and Evolution of Survey Error
detail.abstract:
Surveys provide much of what we know in social science and are often the only source of information on private behaviors, attitudes and expectations. Strands of the literature document four broad error sources: survey coverage, unit non-response, item non-response, and measurement error. Yet the absence of comparable error measures across sources and over time has left the relative severity of error sources difficult to assess, limiting efforts by survey producers to improve accuracy and users to interpret survey statistics. We unify the fragmented literature by analyzing and decomposing survey error in an empirical Total Survey Error (TSE) framework, quantifying for the first time every error component on a common scale of bias and absolute error. We apply our approach to comprehensively measure survey error in eighteen income and program receipt variables from the CPS ASEC – one of the oldest and most rigorously tested surveys, and the official source of income and poverty statistics in the U.S. – using linked administrative records over more than two decades. For nearly half of the variables, bias exceeds 40 percent and eliminating all individual-level error would require changing more than 80 percent of the true total. Contrary to the conventional emphasis on non-response, we find that the dominant source of bias is measurement error among respondents who fail to report receipt (false negatives). The largest potential gains therefore come from improving the accuracy of respondent reporting rather than raising response rates. This underreporting also propagates into imputed values for non-respondents, which are drawn from (misreported) responses and are particularly noisy, with positive and negative errors that tend to offset in net terms. Moreover, net bias can be an incomplete guide to data quality, as we find that absolute error has tended to rise over time even when net bias is stable. Overall, our approach provides a new method for measuring and decomposing survey error, clarifying which sources of bias require user corrections and where survey design improvements could be most consequential.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: Persistence Without Predictive Advantage: Sponsor Histories and Cornerstone Adoption in Hong Kong IPOs

detail.title: Persistence Without Predictive Advantage: Sponsor Histories and Cornerstone Adoption in Hong Kong IPOs

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: Do repeated IPO intermediaries exhibit stable contracting histories, and do those histories improve genuine out-of-time prediction? We study 930 Hong Kong Main Board operating-company IPOs from 2018 through August 2026, 1,524 IPO-sponsor relationships, and 113 canonical sponsor entities. Sponsor histories use only strictly earlier listing dates. At the primary five-prior-deal threshold, the team adoption score has a raw AUC of 0.621 (year-stratified 95% bootstrap interval [0.571, 0.668]; within-year permutation p = 0.0004), while sponsor rankings persist across chronological halves (Spearman ρ = 0.610, p < 0.001). The controlled linear-probability coefficient is 0.390. Its p-value is 0.016 with leadsponsor clustered inference but 0.068 under a 4,999-draw wild-cluster bootstrap. Among single-sponsor IPOs the coefficient is 0.298 (clustered p = 0.081; wild-bootstrap p = 0.147), and omitting CICC reduces the full-team coefficient to 0.263 (p = 0.114). Expanding-window forecasts provide no stable incremental advantage: adding sponsor history changes pooled AUC from 0.691 to 0.682 (difference-0.009; bootstrap interval [-0.035, 0.017]). The difference is +0.030 in 2020-2023 but-0.040 in 2024-2026; the formal history-by-post-2024 interaction is imprecise (p = 0.660). Histories also do not predict release intensity or multi-tranche structure. Sponsor histories are persistent descriptors, but their association is dependence-sensitive and their predictive content becomes redundant as cornerstone adoption diffuses. The evidence is consistent with matching, networks, or routines rather than an exogenous sponsor effect or a portable forecasting advantage.

title: Russian Exhibition Projects as Platforms of Public Diplomacy and a Tool for Constructing the Attractiveness of the National Development Model

detail.title: Russian Exhibition Projects as Platforms of Public Diplomacy and a Tool for Constructing the Attractiveness of the National Development Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Exhibition projects are considered an independent channel of public diplomacy, distinct from interstate negotiation formats and oriented toward direct contact with foreign and domestic audiences. The problem is that exhibition events have long been assigned an auxiliary, predominantly cultural and educational role, while their function in constructing the attractiveness of a national development model has remained outside systematic analysis. The purpose of this study is to determine how major Russian exhibition projects of the first half of the 2020s perform this function and which observable indicators can be used to identify it. The study employs case analysis, comparative and structural-functional methods, as well as secondary analysis of quantitative data on attendance and perceptions of the country brand. The cases are the Russian Pavilion at Expo 2020 Dubai, the International Russia Exhibition-Forum at VDNKh, and the National Centre RUSSIA established on its basis. The analysis shows that the exhibition format combines three operations: demonstrating achievements, engaging visitors, and translating disparate sectoral results into a coherent image of development. Attendance at the Russia Exhibition-Forum exceeded 18.5 million visitors, while Russia's position in the Brand Finance Global Soft Power Index rose to 14th place by 2026. The findings suggest that an exhibition venue functions as a mechanism for assembling a national image from regional and sectoral specifics rather than merely as a showcase of cultural achievements, and that its effectiveness can be assessed through a combination of audience and reputational indicators.

title: Teacher Motivation as the Foundation of Effective School Administration in Nigerian Secondary Schools

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No Conflict of Interest

detail.abstract: This study emphasizes how both intrinsic motivators, such as recognition, professional growth, and job satisfaction, and extrinsic motivators, including salary, working conditions, and job security, affect instructional effectiveness, staff discipline, the overall school climate, and the management of change within schools. Grounded in Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, the theoretical framework highlights the need to balance hygiene factors like adequate remuneration and proper working conditions with motivators that enhance teachers' sense of achievement and professional development. However, several challenges continue to undermine teacher motivation in Nigerian secondary schools. Irregular payment of salaries, inadequate school infrastructure, overcrowded classrooms, and limited access to professional development opportunities act as strong demotivating factors, negatively influencing teacher performance and, consequently, school outcomes. Such challenges often reduce instructional quality, weaken staff discipline, and hinder the implementation of innovative teaching methods and effective school policies. Additionally, the lack of supportive leadership, limited recognition of teachers' contributions, and minimal opportunities for career advancement further erode motivation, creating a cycle of disengagement and low morale. Addressing these issues requires comprehensive strategies that focus on equitable resource allocation, continuous professional development, supportive and participatory leadership, and policy reforms that prioritize teacher welfare. Motivated teachers are essential not only for achieving academic goals but also for fostering a positive school environment that encourages student learning, innovation, and overall institutional growth. By investing in teacher motivation, Nigerian secondary schools can enhance educational quality, improve staff retention, and ensure sustainable school development.

title: The Workflow is not the Work: Executor-contingent Work Decomposition in Human–AI Organizations
affiliations: The Mirandola Institute and

detail.title: The Workflow is not the Work: Executor-contingent Work Decomposition in Human–AI Organizations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Research on artificial intelligence and work commonly asks which existing tasks should be automated, augmented, or retained by humans. That framing often treats the inherited task architecture as the object to be allocated. Agentic artificial intelligence weakens this analytical convenience because artificial executors can use code, application programming interfaces, direct data operations, generated tools, parallel processing, and dynamic production paths that do not reproduce human interfaces, handoffs, or task sequences. We develop a theory of executor-contingent work decomposition: changing executor architecture changes the feasible set of work decompositions, sometimes during execution itself. Machine-native execution can therefore eliminate, combine, relocate, parallelize, and create tasks. It can also redistribute judgment, authority, relational work, and accountability across redesigned job bundles. Reconstruction is bounded by work-decomposition plasticity—the ex ante structural capacity of work to be recombined while preserving necessary causal and constitutive relationships.  We distinguish historical workflow from constitutive process: some inherited steps are implementation conventions, whereas others help make the work valid and must be preserved across alternative paths. Reconstruction can also produce milestone decoupling when reconstructed trajectories cease to map onto the milestones through which managers interpret progress and completion. We introduce governed path equivalence as an acceptance mechanism for unfamiliar paths that preserve required outcomes and constitutive conditions. The framework distinguishes technical divergence, organizational acceptance, and institutionalization, and shows why neither final-output inspection nor inherited-workflow conformity is sufficient for governing machine-native work.

title: An Evaluation of Developed vs Developing Economies: Do Stock Markets Impact Economic Development?
affiliations: Modern School, Barakhamba Road and

detail.title: An Evaluation of Developed vs Developing Economies: Do Stock Markets Impact Economic Development?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: Not applicable

detail.abstract:
Stock markets play a key role in helping businesses raise capital, providing opportunities for
investment, and directing funds where they are needed most. However, the size, stability, and
effectiveness of stock markets vary greatly with a country's level of economic development.
Stock markets in developed economies, such as the New York Stock Exchange, Tokyo Stock
Exchange, and London Stock Exchange, are well-organised and backed by strong legal and
regulatory systems, making them more stable. On the other hand, developing markets like
India's National Stock Exchange and Bombay Stock Exchange are growing quickly but are
more exposed to risks such as political uncertainty, weaker regulations, and investors pulling
out money suddenly. Therefore, this review examines the role and impact of stock markets in
shaping economic development across developed and developing countries. Through an
evaluative approach, the paper analyses how stock markets contribute to capital formation,
investment mobilisation, and economic growth, while highlighting the structural differences
between developed and developing stock markets and comparing how they work, perform, and
respond to major global events, the COVID-19 pandemic, the US-China trade war, and the US-
Iran conflict. Overall, the study highlights the fact that while stock markets are essential drivers
of economic development, their effectiveness depends heavily on institutional strength and
investor confidence. Therefore, strengthening regulatory frameworks and improving market
resilience in developing economies can help reduce vulnerability to global shocks.

title: Where Do the Male Chicks From Layer Lines Go? A Critical Review of the Economic Fate of Male Chicks in the Poultry Egg Industry, Their Animal-Protein Potential, and the Data Gap in Türkiye

detail.title: Where Do the Male Chicks From Layer Lines Go? A Critical Review of the Economic Fate of Male Chicks in the Poultry Egg Industry, Their Animal-Protein Potential, and the Data Gap in Türkiye

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no personal, professional, or financial relationships that could have influenced, or could reasonably be perceived to have influenced, this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it is a literature review and research problem analysis based exclusively on previously published sources and publicly available information. No human participants or animals were directly involved in the research.

detail.abstract: Modern poultry production has become increasingly divided into genetically specialized lines for egg and meat production. This specialization has turned male chicks born from laying strains into a production surplus that is economically and ethically contentious. While both male and female broilers can be incorporated into commercial meat production, males from layer genetic lines are unable to compete with broiler strains in terms of growth rate and carcass yield. Consequently, the culling of day-old male layer chicks at the hatchery stage has long been practiced in many countries. More recently, alternatives such as in ovo sex determination, dual-purpose breeds, and rearing male layer chicks for meat production have gained attention. This study critically reviews the position of male chicks from layer lines within the production chain from the perspectives of animal welfare, production economics, animal by-products, and protein recovery. The central research question is: What is the ultimate economic fate of male chicks originating from layer lines that do not directly enter the commercial broiler-meat chain? The literature review indicates that treating male layer chicks solely as "waste" is scientifically insufficient. Some studies have investigated the production of chick meal from day-old male chicks and its use as an animal-protein concentrate, while other studies have demonstrated that male layer chickens can be used directly for meat production. However, the economic feasibility of these alternatives varies according to national conditions, production systems, and regulatory frameworks. For Türkiye, the most important finding is that although regulations exist concerning the culling and disposal of hatchery-origin chicks, no publicly accessible, systematic, and verifiable dataset was identified that documents the annual number of male chicks originating from layer lines and their ultimate fate after culling. Therefore, no definitive conclusion can be drawn regarding the extent to which this material is utilized in Türkiye through feed, animal protein, rendering, pet food, fertilizer, or other industrial channels. The study argues that this data gap constitutes an important research field not only in terms of animal welfare, but also with regard to the circular economy, resource efficiency, animal-protein production, and transparency in food systems.

title: Before the Breaking Point: Beyond the Critical Incident—Integrating Psychological First Aid Into First Responder Support

detail.title: Before the Breaking Point: Beyond the Critical Incident—Integrating Psychological First Aid Into First Responder Support

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.

detail.abstract: First responders routinely operate in environments characterized by uncertainty, human suffering, operational responsibility, and repeated exposure to potentially stressful events. Organizational psychological-support systems, however, may become most visible only following formally recognized critical incidents or after responder distress has become sufficiently apparent to trigger intervention. This white paper examines how principles associated with Psychological First Aid (PFA) can inform a broader, proactive approach to psychological support for emergency medical services personnel, firefighters, law-enforcement personnel, emergency dispatchers and telecommunicators, and other frontline public-safety professionals. PFA is considered not as psychotherapy, diagnosis, or a substitute for professional behavioral-health care, but as one component within a continuum that may also include practical assistance, peer support, supportive supervision, Stress First Aid or comparable occupational frameworks, professional referral, treatment, and emergency intervention when appropriate. Particular attention is given to cumulative occupational exposure, organizational culture, psychological safety, leadership, practical workplace conditions, confidentiality, responder autonomy, referral pathways, resilience, and the boundaries between supportive and clinical care. The evidence reviewed indicates important limitations in the responder-specific PFA, peer-support, and organizational-intervention literature and does not support claims that PFA-informed systems prevent specific psychiatric outcomes. Nevertheless, the analysis supports an organizational shift away from relying exclusively on post-crisis intervention and toward building accessible, bounded, evidence-informed systems capable of connecting responders with appropriate levels of support earlier. Responder resilience is therefore framed as a shared responsibility in which individual capacity and organizational conditions reinforce rather than replace one another. The central practice implication is that public-safety organizations should develop support capability before responder distress must become a crisis to receive meaningful attention.

detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of the umrah industry has increased the demand for competent mutawwif who are capable of providing both religious guidance and professional operational services. Although Malaysia's National Occupational Skills Standard (NOSS) offers a competencybased framework within Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), its responsiveness to contemporary industry requirements remains underexplored. This study aims to analyse the structure and content of NOSS-based mutawwif competency modules and to propose an Industry-Responsive Mutawwif Competency Model (IRMCM) that supports sustainable human capital development in the umrah industry. A qualitative document analysis was employed to examine Level 3 and Level 4 NOSS competency modules together with relevant policy and industry documents. Data were analysed using content and thematic analyses to identify competency domains, structural characteristics, and gaps between existing training provisions and current industry needs. The findings reveal that the modules are well aligned with competency-based training (CBT) and TVET principles, particularly in developing religious knowledge and foundational competencies. However, significant gaps remain in digital literacy, operational management, professional communication, risk management, and adaptive competencies required by the contemporary umrah industry. In response, this study proposes the IRMCM, which integrates religious, operational, digital, communication, and adaptive competencies into a comprehensive competency framework. The proposed model extends existing TVET competency frameworks by incorporating sustainability-oriented workforce capabilities and provides practical guidance for curriculum enhancement, policy development, and professional training. It also contributes to sustainable human capital development by supporting Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4 (Quality Education) and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) within the Islamic tourism sector.

detail.abstract: If you have HK$20,000 in idle capital and want to start investing, opening online forums or social media often reveals a group of "popular online quant model promoters" recommending multi-asset leveraged hedging, splitting capital into 6 ETFs to execute Return Stacking, claiming this to be the ultimate secret code for "extremely low risk, smoothed volatility, and high Sharpe ratio." detail.abstract: This study develops selective home-country governance to explain how China's Encouraged-Restricted-Prohibited (ERP) framework shapes overseas projects. Building on the Ownership-Location-Internalisation (OLI) paradigm, it argues that firm capabilities, host-country conditions, and governance choices make internationalisation economically attractive, whereas home-country policy influences which configurations proceed. Using project-level China Global Investment Tracker data, the analysis compares three Going Global periods through annualised measures, portfolio comparisons, and a secondary difference-indifferences analysis. The post-ERP period maintained substantial activity within a more selective portfolio. Restricted or sensitive activities lost prominence, while transport, greenfield, and Belt and Road Initiative-related projects gained importance. Typical project value changed modestly, and the exposure analysis found no distinct post-ERP reduction among restricted or sensitive transactions. The findings locate the principal adjustment in project frequency and portfolio composition, showing how selective home-country governance conditions the implementation of OLI configurations.

detail.abstract: This paper examines when artificial intelligence (AI) generates value for multinational enterprises in the global integrated circuit industry. It argues that AI enhances firm performance by empowering managers to tackle circuit layout, fabrication, supply disruptions, and partner coordination across dispersed operations. The study shows that firms do not derive a competitive advantage from simply possessing advanced technologies, but rather by actively integrating prior learning with evolving organizational and value-chain requirements. Drawing on the knowledgebased view and dynamic capability theory, the paper conceptualizes prior learning as an input into combinative innovation. The analysis uses patent data to provide observable indicators of this process. The empirical results remain stable across various model specifications and robustness checks, including fixed-effects count models, logged specifications, within-between estimation, narrower variable definitions, interaction models, portfolio reconfiguration tests, placebo tests, and alternative depreciation rates. Across all models, firms with stronger prior activity are more likely to generate combinative innovations, especially when they possess deeper complementary semiconductor capabilities. Current combinative innovation predicts future portfolio renewal. The results demonstrate that firms derive competitive advantage in complex, global production networks by repeatedly recombining knowledge across domains, rather than from static ownership of technological assets.

detail.abstract: As Western culture evolves, missionaries from the West are facing new challenges. These challenges can be observed in the North American churches where many of these missionaries were raised. In this study, we seek to understand what the greatest challenges for church leaders (including missionaries) are, how they relate to age, and how this information can benefit missionaries, especially church-planting missionaries. In this study, North American church leaders (N = 347) indicated how great 79 commonly faced challenges were perceived to be, as well as their age and information about their church's size and growth. A factor analysis reduced these 79 challenges to 16 clusters of challenges. Six of these clusters were related to age. Older leaders found maintaining their mental health, self-management, and church finances less challenging than did younger leaders. The differences in mental health were especially strong. In contrast, younger church leaders found evangelism, creating effective programs, and addressing problems associated with social media use less challenging than did older leaders. Moreover, churches with younger leaders were growing faster than churches with older leaders. The cultural dynamics producing these differences in North American churches are likely to act on missionary teams comprised of North Americans. For older and younger missionaries to benefit from each other's strengths, it might be beneficial for both older and younger missionaries to form teams together.
